Al-Bukhari and others narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Banu Isra'il, al-Kahf, Maryam and al-Anbiya' are among the first of the old (*'ataq*) surahs, and they are part of my ancient possessions (*tilad*)." Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu'aym, in *al-Hilya*, narrated from 'Amir ibn Rabi'a that a man from the Arabs stayed with him, and 'Amir honoured his lodging. 'Amir then spoke on the man's behalf to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The man came to 'Amir and said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a valley, and there is no valley among the Arabs better than it. I wanted to grant you a portion of it, to be yours and your descendants' after you." 'Amir said: "I have no need of your portion. A surah was revealed today that has made us forget the world: ﴿The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they are heedless, turning away﴾."

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they are heedless, turning away.﴾ ﴿No fresh reminder comes to them from their Lord but they listen to it while playing.﴾ ﴿Their hearts are distracted. And the wrongdoers conspire in secret, saying, "Is this not but a human like you? Will you then go to magic while you see?"﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."﴾ ﴿But they said, "Confused dreams!" "Rather, he has invented it!" "Rather, he is a poet! Let him bring us a sign as the earlier messengers were sent."﴾ ﴿No town that We destroyed before them believed. Will they then believe?﴾ ﴿We did not send before you any but men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of the reminder, if you do not know.﴾ ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal.﴾ ﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them, and We saved them and whom We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors.﴾

The meaning of the reckoning's time drawing near is that it approaches them, because at every moment it is closer to them than the moment before. It is also said that everything that is coming is near, and the death of every person is the establishment of his hour; the Resurrection is also near in comparison with the time that has passed, since what remains of the world is less than what has passed. "The people" is general in meaning. It is also said that it refers to the polytheists in general, and it is said that it refers to the disbelievers of Makkah. On this view, it is said that "the reckoning" means their punishment on the Day of Badr. The description of the reminder as *muhdath* ("fresh" or "newly created") has been used as evidence that the Qur'an is created (*muhdath*), since the reminder here is the Qur'an. What happened to Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal of severe beating and long imprisonment happened; and because of it, the neck of Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Khuza'i was struck, and a great trial arose at that time and after it. They went further to declaring disbelief in whoever abstained (*waqf*). Would that they had not exceeded the limit of abstention and returning knowledge to the Knower of the unseen, for nothing of the kind of speech about this question was heard from the righteous predecessors, the Companions, the Successors and those after them, until the time of the trial and the appearance of this discussion. Nor was any word on it transmitted from them. Therefore, refraining from complying with what they called for, holding firmly to the skirts of abstention, and returning the knowledge of this to its Knower is the best course. In it is safety and freedom from declaring disbelief in groups of Allah's servants. The matter belongs to Allah, glorified is He.

His saying ﴿but they listen to it﴾ is a fully detached exception (*istithna' mufarragh*) in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause. The meaning is: no fresh reminder comes to them from their Lord at any state except that they listen to it along with play, mockery and the distraction of the hearts. It is said that it is in the nominative position as a substitute (*badal*) for the *waw* in *asarru*; this was said by al-Mubarrad and others. It is said that it is in the nominative position by way of vituperation (*dhamm*). It is said that it is the subject of an omitted verb, the implied meaning being "those who wronged said," and al-Nahhas preferred this. It is said that it is in the accusative position with the implied verb "I mean." It is said that it is in the genitive position as a substitute for *al-nas* ("the people"); al-Mubarrad mentioned this. It is said that it is in the nominative position as the subject of *asarru*, according to the dialect of those who permit two subjects together, like their saying *akalunī al-baraghīth* ("the fleas ate me"); al-Akhfash mentioned this. Similar to it is ﴿Then they were blind and deaf, many of them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 71]. From the same is the poet's saying:

*So the she-mules found their way to the targets.*

And the saying of another:

*But his father and mother drew near to me,*
*at Hawran, where his relatives press the pure oil.*

Al-Kisa'i said: there is inversion in it, that is: "And those who wronged conspired in secret." Abu 'Ubaydah said: *asarru* here is one of the words with opposite meanings: it may mean they concealed their speech, and it may mean they made it public and declared it. ﴿Is this not but a human like you?﴾ This sentence is with an implied "saying" before it: that is, they said, "Is this messenger not but a human like you, who is not distinguished from you by anything?" It is also permissible for this sentence to be a substitute for *al-najwa*, and *hal* here has the sense of negation: that is, and they conspired this talk in secret. The interrogative *hamza* in ﴿Will you then go to magic﴾ is for denunciation, and the *fa'* is for coordination with an implied element, as in its parallels. The clause ﴿while you see﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause. The meaning: if he is a human like you, and what he brought is magic, how can you respond to him and follow him? So Allah informed His Prophet (ﷺ) of what they whispered.

Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to answer them, and so He said: ﴿He said, "My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth"﴾, that is, nothing that is said in them is hidden from Him. In the codices of the people of Kufa it is "He said, *My Lord*," meaning Muhammad said, "My Lord knows the word, so He knows what you have conspired." It was said that the first reading is preferable, because they concealed this speech, so Allah informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of it and commanded him to say this to them. Al-Nahhas said: both readings are sound, and they are like two verses. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾: He hears everything that is heard and knows everything that is known, so this includes what they concealed, entering it at the first level. ﴿But they said, "Confused dreams!"﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: that is, they said that what he brings is confused dreams. Al-Qutaybi said: *adghath al-ahlam* are false visions. Al-Yazidi said: *al-adghath* are whatever has no interpretation. This is a turning away from Allah's side, glorified is He, relating what occurred from them, and a shift from relating their earlier saying to relating this statement. Then He, glorified is He, related their turning from their saying "confused dreams": He said, "Rather, he has invented it," that is, they said, "Rather, he has invented it on his own, with no basis." Then He, glorified is He, related that they turned from this and said, "Rather, he is a poet," and what he brought is of the kind of poetry. In this confusion, vacillation and indecision on their part is the greatest proof that they were ignorant of the reality of what he brought; they did not know what it was and did not recognize its nature. Or they knew that it was true and that it was from Allah, but they wanted to repel it with words and pelt it with every stone and clod, and this is the condition of one who has been overcome by proof and subdued by evidence. Then after all this, they said: ﴿Let him bring us a sign﴾; this is the answer to an omitted conditional: that is, if it is not as we have said, then let him bring us a sign ﴿as the earlier messengers were sent﴾, that is, as Musa was sent with the staff and other things, and Salih with the she-camel. The position of the *kaf* is genitive as an adjective of *ayah* (sign). It is also permissible for it to be an adjective of an omitted verbal noun. Their request was a request of obstinacy, because Allah, glorified is He, had already given them signs sufficient for them. Had Allah known that they would believe if He gave them what they proposed, He would have given it to them, as He said: ﴿Had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear; and had He made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse﴾ [al-Anfal: 23]. Al-Zajjaj said: they proposed signs after which there would be no respite.

Then Allah answered them: ﴿No town that We destroyed before them believed﴾, that is, before the polytheists of Makkah. The meaning of *min qaryah* is "from the people of a town." He described the town by His saying *ahlaknaha*, that is, We destroyed its people, or We destroyed it by destroying its people. In this is an explanation that Allah's way with past nations was that when those who made proposals were given what they proposed and then did not believe, the punishment of annihilation descended upon them without doubt. The *min* in *min qaryah* is superfluous, for emphasis. The meaning: no town of those towns which We destroyed, because of their proposals, believed before these people; so how would We give them what they propose, when they are the model of those before them? The interrogative *hamza* in ﴿Will they then believe?﴾ is for rebuke and reproach. The meaning: if a nation of the destroyed nations did not believe when given what they proposed, how would these people believe if they were given what they proposed?

Then He, glorified is He, answered their saying "Is this not but a human like you?" with His saying: ﴿We did not send before you any but men to whom We revealed﴾, that is, We did not send before you to the earlier nations except men from among mankind, and We did not send angels to them, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Say, "If there were angels walking calmly on the earth, We would have sent down upon them from the sky an angel as a messenger"﴾ [al-Isra': 95]. The clause ﴿to whom We revealed﴾ is a resumptive clause (*mustaanafah*) explaining the manner of sending, and it is also permissible for it to be an adjective of *rijalan*, that is, characterized by the attribute of revelation to them. Hafs, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *nuhi* with the *nun*, and the rest read it with the *ya'* (the lower dotted letter). Then Allah commanded them to ask the people of the reminder if they were ignorant of this, so He said: ﴿So ask the people of the reminder, if you do not know.﴾ The people of the reminder are the people of the two Scriptures: the Jews and the Christians. The meaning of ﴿if you do not know﴾ is: if you do not know that the messengers of Allah are human. So said most of the commentators. But the Jews and the Christians were not ignorant of this and did not deny it. The sense of the sentence is: if you do not know what has been mentioned, then ask the people of the reminder. The verse has been cited as evidence that *taqlid* (blind imitation) is permissible, and this is a mistake. Even if it were granted, the meaning would be asking them about the texts of the Book and the Sunnah, not about pure opinion. *Taqlid* is nothing but accepting the saying of another without his proof. We have clarified this in a short treatise, which we named *al-Qawl al-Mufid fi Hukm al-Taqlid* ("The Beneficial Word on the Ruling on Taqlid").

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 21, verses 1–9 (part 2 of 2):

Then, when He, glory be to Him, had finished answering their doubt, He emphasized that the Messengers are of the same kind as human beings, and so He said: ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food﴾. That is, the Messengers are a model for the rest of the children of Adam in the judgment of nature: they eat as they eat and drink as they drink. "Jasad" (body) is the physical form of a human being. Al-Zajjaj said: it is singular, but it refers to a plurality, meaning "jasad" indicates a group; that is, "We did not make them possessors of bodies that do not eat food." Thus the clause ﴿that do not eat food﴾ is a description of "jasadan" (a body): that is, "We did not make them a body that is independent of eating, but rather it is in need of that." ﴿Nor were they immortal﴾, but they die as other human beings die, and they (the disbelievers) had believed that the Messengers do not die, so God answered them with this.

The clause ﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them﴾ is conjoined to a clause indicated by the context, and the implied sense is: "We revealed to them what We revealed, then We fulfilled the promise to them," that is, We carried out the promise We had made them of delivering them and destroying those who denied them. For this reason He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿So We delivered them and whom We willed﴾ of Our believing servants, and what is meant is their deliverance from the punishment, and the destruction of those who disbelieved by worldly punishment. By "the transgressors" (al-musrifin) is meant those who exceed the limit in disbelief and sins, and they are the polytheists.

Al-Nasa'i reported from Abu Sa'id, "from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning His saying: ﴿And they are heedless, turning away﴾, he said: 'In this world.'" Ibn Mardawayh reported from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the verse, he said: "From the affairs of this world." Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Qatadah concerning His saying: ﴿Nay, they say: a confusion of dreams﴾, that is, the act of dreams, and it is only a vision he saw; ﴿Nay, he has invented it; nay, he is a poet﴾, all of this was said by him; ﴿Let him bring us a sign as the first ones were sent﴾, as 'Isa and Musa brought clear proofs and messengers; ﴿No town We destroyed before them believed﴾, that is, when the Messengers came to their peoples with clear proofs and they did not believe, they were not given respite. Ibn Jarir reported from Qatadah, who said: "The people of Makkah said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'If what you say is true, and it would please you that we believe, then turn Safa into gold for us.' Then Jibril came to him and said: 'If you wish, it will be what your people asked, but if they then do not believe, they will not be given respite; and if you wish, you may give your people more time.' He said: 'Rather, I will give my people more time.' So God revealed: ﴿No town before them believed﴾," the verse.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food﴾, he says: We did not make them bodies that do not eat food; rather, We made them bodies that eat food.

Al-Bukhari and others narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Banu Isra'il, al-Kahf, Maryam and al-Anbiya' are among the first of the old (*'ataq*) surahs, and they are part of my ancient possessions (*tilad*)." I wanted to grant you a portion of it, to be yours and your descendants' after you." 'Amir said: "I have no need of your portion. A surah was revealed today that has made us forget the world: ﴿The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they are heedless, turning away﴾."

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Then, when He, glory be to Him, had finished answering their doubt, He emphasized that the Messengers are of the same kind as human beings, and so He said: ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food﴾. That is, the Messengers are a model for the rest of the children of Adam in the judgment of nature: they eat as they eat and drink as they drink. "Jasad" (body) is the physical form of a human being. Al-Zajjaj said: it is singular, but it refers to a plurality, meaning "jasad" indicates a group; that is, "We did not make them possessors of bodies that do not eat food." In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they are heedless, turning away.﴾ ﴿No fresh reminder comes to them from their Lord but they listen to it while playing.﴾ ﴿Their hearts are distracted. And the wrongdoers conspire in secret, saying, "Is this not but a human like you? Will you then go to magic while you see?"﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."﴾ ﴿But they said, "Confused dreams!" "Rather, he has invented it!" "Rather, he is a poet! Let him bring us a sign as the earlier messengers were sent."﴾ ﴿No town that We destroyed before them believed. Will they then believe?﴾ ﴿We did not send before you any but men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of the reminder, if you do not know.﴾ ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal.﴾ ﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them, and We saved them and whom We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors.﴾

The meaning of the reckoning's time drawing near is that it approaches them, because at every moment it is closer to them than the moment before. It is also said that everything that is coming is near, and the death of every person is the establishment of his hour; the Resurrection is also near in comparison with the time that has passed, since what remains of the world is less than what has passed. "The people" is general in meaning. It is also said that it refers to the polytheists in general, and it is said that it refers to the disbelievers of Makkah. The description of the reminder as *muhdath* ("fresh" or "newly created") has been used as evidence that the Qur'an is created (*muhdath*), since the reminder here is the Qur'an. It is answered that there is no dispute about the createdness of a composition made of sounds and letters, since it is renewed in its descent; so the meaning is that its sending down is newly created. The dispute is only about the inner speech (*al-kalam al-nafsi*). This question, namely the eternity or createdness of the Qur'an, afflicted many scholars and virtuous men in the era of the Ma'mun, the Mu'tasim and the Wathiq. What happened to Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal of severe beating and long imprisonment happened; and because of it, the neck of Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Khuza'i was struck, and a great trial arose at that time and after it. The story is too famous to be recounted. Whoever wishes to learn its truth should consult the biography of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal in *Siyar A'lam al-Nubala'* by the historian of Islam al-Dhahabi. In it is safety and freedom from declaring disbelief in groups of Allah's servants. The matter belongs to Allah, glorified is He.

His saying ﴿but they listen to it﴾ is a fully detached exception (*istithna' mufarragh*) in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause. It is said that it is in the nominative position as a substitute (*badal*) for the *waw* in *asarru*; this was said by al-Mubarrad and others. It is said that it is in the nominative position by way of vituperation (*dhamm*). It is said that it is the subject of an omitted verb, the implied meaning being "those who wronged said," and al-Nahhas preferred this. It is said that it is in the accusative position with the implied verb "I mean." It is said that it is in the genitive position as a substitute for *al-nas* ("the people"); al-Mubarrad mentioned this. It is said that it is in the nominative position as the subject of *asarru*, according to the dialect of those who permit two subjects together, like their saying *akalunī al-baraghīth* ("the fleas ate me"); al-Akhfash mentioned this. Similar to it is ﴿Then they were blind and deaf, many of them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 71]. From the same is the poet's saying:

*So the she-mules found their way to the targets.*

And the saying of another:

*But his father and mother drew near to me,*
*at Hawran, where his relatives press the pure oil.*

Al-Kisa'i said: there is inversion in it, that is: "And those who wronged conspired in secret." Abu 'Ubaydah said: *asarru* here is one of the words with opposite meanings: it may mean they concealed their speech, and it may mean they made it public and declared it. ﴿Is this not but a human like you?﴾ This sentence is with an implied "saying" before it: that is, they said, "Is this messenger not but a human like you, who is not distinguished from you by anything?" It is also permissible for this sentence to be a substitute for *al-najwa*, and *hal* here has the sense of negation: that is, and they conspired this talk in secret. The interrogative *hamza* in ﴿Will you then go to magic﴾ is for denunciation, and the *fa'* is for coordination with an implied element, as in its parallels. The clause ﴿while you see﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause. The meaning: if he is a human like you, and what he brought is magic, how can you respond to him and follow him? So Allah informed His Prophet (ﷺ) of what they whispered.

Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to answer them, and so He said: ﴿He said, "My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth"﴾, that is, nothing that is said in them is hidden from Him. In the codices of the people of Kufa it is "He said, *My Lord*," meaning Muhammad said, "My Lord knows the word, so He knows what you have conspired." It was said that the first reading is preferable, because they concealed this speech, so Allah informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of it and commanded him to say this to them. Then He, glorified is He, related their turning from their saying "confused dreams": He said, "Rather, he has invented it," that is, they said, "Rather, he has invented it on his own, with no basis." Then He, glorified is He, related that they turned from this and said, "Rather, he is a poet," and what he brought is of the kind of poetry. In this confusion, vacillation and indecision on their part is the greatest proof that they were ignorant of the reality of what he brought; they did not know what it was and did not recognize its nature. It is said that it is in the nominative position as a substitute (*badal*) for the *waw* in *asarru*; this was said by al-Mubarrad and others. It is said that it is in the nominative position by way of vituperation (*dhamm*). It is said that it is the subject of an omitted verb, the implied meaning being "those who wronged said," and al-Nahhas preferred this. It is said that it is in the accusative position with the implied verb "I mean." It is said that it is in the genitive position as a substitute for *al-nas* ("the people"); al-Mubarrad mentioned this. It is said that it is in the nominative position as the subject of *asarru*, according to the dialect of those who permit two subjects together, like their saying *akalunī al-baraghīth* ("the fleas ate me"); al-Akhfash mentioned this. Similar to it is ﴿Then they were blind and deaf, many of them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 71]. From the same is the poet's saying:

*So the she-mules found their way to the targets.*

And the saying of another:

*But his father and mother drew near to me,*
*at Hawran, where his relatives press the pure oil.*

Al-Kisa'i said: there is inversion in it, that is: "And those who wronged conspired in secret." Abu 'Ubaydah said: *asarru* here is one of the words with opposite meanings: it may mean they concealed their speech, and it may mean they made it public and declared it. ﴿Is this not but a human like you?﴾ This sentence is with an implied "saying" before it: that is, they said, "Is this messenger not but a human like you, who is not distinguished from you by anything?" It is also permissible for this sentence to be a substitute for *al-najwa*, and *hal* here has the sense of negation: that is, and they conspired this talk in secret. The clause ﴿while you see﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause. The meaning: if he is a human like you, and what he brought is magic, how can you respond to him and follow him? So Allah informed His Prophet (ﷺ) of what they whispered.

Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to answer them, and so He said: ﴿He said, "My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth"﴾, that is, nothing that is said in them is hidden from Him. In the codices of the people of Kufa it is "He said, *My Lord*," meaning Muhammad said, "My Lord knows the word, so He knows what you have conspired." It was said that the first reading is preferable, because they concealed this speech, so Allah informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of it and commanded him to say this to them. Al-Nahhas said: both readings are sound, and they are like two verses. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾: He hears everything that is heard and knows everything that is known, so this includes what they concealed, entering it at the first level. ﴿But they said, "Confused dreams!"﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: that is, they said that what he brings is confused dreams. Had Allah known that they would believe if He gave them what they proposed, He would have given it to them, as He said: ﴿Had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear; and had He made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse﴾ [al-Anfal: 23]. Then Allah answered them: ﴿No town that We destroyed before them believed﴾, that is, before the polytheists of Makkah. The meaning of *min qaryah* is "from the people of a town." He described the town by His saying *ahlaknaha*, that is, We destroyed its people, or We destroyed it by destroying its people. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

This question, namely the eternity or createdness of the Qur'an, afflicted many scholars and virtuous men in the era of the Ma'mun, the Mu'tasim and the Wathiq. What happened to Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal of severe beating and long imprisonment happened; and because of it, the neck of Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Khuza'i was struck, and a great trial arose at that time and after it. The man came to 'Amir and said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a valley, and there is no valley among the Arabs better than it. I wanted to grant you a portion of it, to be yours and your descendants' after you." 'Amir said: "I have no need of your portion. A surah was revealed today that has made us forget the world: ﴿The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they are heedless, turning away﴾."

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they are heedless, turning away.﴾ ﴿No fresh reminder comes to them from their Lord but they listen to it while playing.﴾ ﴿Their hearts are distracted. And the wrongdoers conspire in secret, saying, "Is this not but a human like you? Will you then go to magic while you see?"﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."﴾ ﴿But they said, "Confused dreams!" "Rather, he has invented it!" "Rather, he is a poet! Let him bring us a sign as the earlier messengers were sent."﴾ ﴿No town that We destroyed before them believed. Will they then believe?﴾ ﴿We did not send before you any but men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of the reminder, if you do not know.﴾ ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal.﴾ ﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them, and We saved them and whom We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors.﴾

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of ﴿has drawn near for the people﴾ is the time of their reckoning, that is, the Resurrection, as in His saying: ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾ [al-Qamar: 1]. The *lam* in *li-l-nas* is connected to the verb, and placing it and its genitive object before the subject is for the sake of emphasis and awe. The meaning of the reckoning's time drawing near is that it approaches them, because at every moment it is closer to them than the moment before. It is also said that everything that is coming is near, and the death of every person is the establishment of his hour; the Resurrection is also near in comparison with the time that has passed, since what remains of the world is less than what has passed. "The people" is general in meaning. It is also said that it refers to the polytheists in general, and it is said that it refers to the disbelievers of Makkah. On this view, it is said that "the reckoning" means their punishment on the Day of Badr. The description of the reminder as *muhdath* ("fresh" or "newly created") has been used as evidence that the Qur'an is created (*muhdath*), since the reminder here is the Qur'an. It is answered that there is no dispute about the createdness of a composition made of sounds and letters, since it is renewed in its descent; so the meaning is that its sending down is newly created. The dispute is only about the inner speech (*al-kalam al-nafsi*). This question, namely the eternity or createdness of the Qur'an, afflicted many scholars and virtuous men in the era of the Ma'mun, the Mu'tasim and the Wathiq. What happened to Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal of severe beating and long imprisonment happened; and because of it, the neck of Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Khuza'i was struck, and a great trial arose at that time and after it. The story is too famous to be recounted. Whoever wishes to learn its truth should consult the biography of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal in *Siyar A'lam al-Nubala'* by the historian of Islam al-Dhahabi. However, may Allah have mercy on them, they went beyond that to a firm assertion of its eternity, and did not stop there until they declared disbelief in whoever said it was created. They went further to declaring disbelief in whoever abstained (*waqf*). Would that they had not exceeded the limit of abstention and returning knowledge to the Knower of the unseen, for nothing of the kind of speech about this question was heard from the righteous predecessors, the Companions, the Successors and those after them, until the time of the trial and the appearance of this discussion. Nor was any word on it transmitted from them. Therefore, refraining from complying with what they called for, holding firmly to the skirts of abstention, and returning the knowledge of this to its Knower is the best course. In it is safety and freedom from declaring disbelief in groups of Allah's servants. The matter belongs to Allah, glorified is He.

His saying ﴿but they listen to it﴾ is a fully detached exception (*istithna' mufarragh*) in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause. The clause ﴿while they play﴾ is also in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause, from the doer of *istama'uhu* ("they listened to it"). ﴿Their hearts are distracted﴾ is also a circumstantial clause. The meaning is: no fresh reminder comes to them from their Lord at any state except that they listen to it along with play, mockery and the distraction of the hearts. It is said that it is in the nominative position as a substitute (*badal*) for the *waw* in *asarru*; this was said by al-Mubarrad and others. It is said that it is in the nominative position by way of vituperation (*dhamm*). It is said that it is the subject of an omitted verb, the implied meaning being "those who wronged said," and al-Nahhas preferred this. It is said that it is in the accusative position with the implied verb "I mean." It is said that it is in the genitive position as a substitute for *al-nas* ("the people"); al-Mubarrad mentioned this. It is said that it is in the nominative position as the subject of *asarru*, according to the dialect of those who permit two subjects together, like their saying *akalunī al-baraghīth* ("the fleas ate me"); al-Akhfash mentioned this. Similar to it is ﴿Then they were blind and deaf, many of them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 71]. From the same is the poet's saying:

*So the she-mules found their way to the targets.*

And the saying of another:

*But his father and mother drew near to me,*
*at Hawran, where his relatives press the pure oil.*

Al-Kisa'i said: there is inversion in it, that is: "And those who wronged conspired in secret." Abu 'Ubaydah said: *asarru* here is one of the words with opposite meanings: it may mean they concealed their speech, and it may mean they made it public and declared it. ﴿Is this not but a human like you?﴾ This sentence is with an implied "saying" before it: that is, they said, "Is this messenger not but a human like you, who is not distinguished from you by anything?" It is also permissible for this sentence to be a substitute for *al-najwa*, and *hal* here has the sense of negation: that is, and they conspired this talk in secret. The interrogative *hamza* in ﴿Will you then go to magic﴾ is for denunciation, and the *fa'* is for coordination with an implied element, as in its parallels. The clause ﴿while you see﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause. The meaning: if he is a human like you, and what he brought is magic, how can you respond to him and follow him? So Allah informed His Prophet (ﷺ) of what they whispered.

Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to answer them, and so He said: ﴿He said, "My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth"﴾, that is, nothing that is said in them is hidden from Him. In the codices of the people of Kufa it is "He said, *My Lord*," meaning Muhammad said, "My Lord knows the word, so He knows what you have conspired." It was said that the first reading is preferable, because they concealed this speech, so Allah informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of it and commanded him to say this to them. Al-Nahhas said: both readings are sound, and they are like two verses. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾: He hears everything that is heard and knows everything that is known, so this includes what they concealed, entering it at the first level. ﴿But they said, "Confused dreams!"﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: that is, they said that what he brings is confused dreams. Al-Qutaybi said: *adghath al-ahlam* are false visions. Al-Yazidi said: *al-adghath* are whatever has no interpretation. This is a turning away from Allah's side, glorified is He, relating what occurred from them, and a shift from relating their earlier saying to relating this statement. Then He, glorified is He, related their turning from their saying "confused dreams": He said, "Rather, he has invented it," that is, they said, "Rather, he has invented it on his own, with no basis." Then He, glorified is He, related that they turned from this and said, "Rather, he is a poet," and what he brought is of the kind of poetry. In this confusion, vacillation and indecision on their part is the greatest proof that they were ignorant of the reality of what he brought; they did not know what it was and did not recognize its nature. Or they knew that it was true and that it was from Allah, but they wanted to repel it with words and pelt it with every stone and clod, and this is the condition of one who has been overcome by proof and subdued by evidence. Then after all this, they said: ﴿Let him bring us a sign﴾; this is the answer to an omitted conditional: that is, if it is not as we have said, then let him bring us a sign ﴿as the earlier messengers were sent﴾, that is, as Musa was sent with the staff and other things, and Salih with the she-camel. The position of the *kaf* is genitive as an adjective of *ayah* (sign). It is also permissible for it to be an adjective of an omitted verbal noun. Their request was a request of obstinacy, because Allah, glorified is He, had already given them signs sufficient for them. Had Allah known that they would believe if He gave them what they proposed, He would have given it to them, as He said: ﴿Had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear; and had He made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse﴾ [al-Anfal: 23]. Al-Zajjaj said: they proposed signs after which there would be no respite.

Then Allah answered them: ﴿No town that We destroyed before them believed﴾, that is, before the polytheists of Makkah. The meaning of *min qaryah* is "from the people of a town." He described the town by His saying *ahlaknaha*, that is, We destroyed its people, or We destroyed it by destroying its people. In this is an explanation that Allah's way with past nations was that when those who made proposals were given what they proposed and then did not believe, the punishment of annihilation descended upon them without doubt. The *min* in *min qaryah* is superfluous, for emphasis. The meaning: no town of those towns which We destroyed, because of their proposals, believed before these people; so how would We give them what they propose, when they are the model of those before them? The interrogative *hamza* in ﴿Will they then believe?﴾ is for rebuke and reproach. The meaning: if a nation of the destroyed nations did not believe when given what they proposed, how would these people believe if they were given what they proposed?

Then He, glorified is He, answered their saying "Is this not but a human like you?" with His saying: ﴿We did not send before you any but men to whom We revealed﴾, that is, We did not send before you to the earlier nations except men from among mankind, and We did not send angels to them, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Say, "If there were angels walking calmly on the earth, We would have sent down upon them from the sky an angel as a messenger"﴾ [al-Isra': 95]. The clause ﴿to whom We revealed﴾ is a resumptive clause (*mustaanafah*) explaining the manner of sending, and it is also permissible for it to be an adjective of *rijalan*, that is, characterized by the attribute of revelation to them. Hafs, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *nuhi* with the *nun*, and the rest read it with the *ya'* (the lower dotted letter). Then Allah commanded them to ask the people of the reminder if they were ignorant of this, so He said: ﴿So ask the people of the reminder, if you do not know.﴾ The people of the reminder are the people of the two Scriptures: the Jews and the Christians. The meaning of ﴿if you do not know﴾ is: if you do not know that the messengers of Allah are human. So said most of the commentators. But the Jews and the Christians were not ignorant of this and did not deny it. The sense of the sentence is: if you do not know what has been mentioned, then ask the people of the reminder. The verse has been cited as evidence that *taqlid* (blind imitation) is permissible, and this is a mistake. Even if it were granted, the meaning would be asking them about the texts of the Book and the Sunnah, not about pure opinion. *Taqlid* is nothing but accepting the saying of another without his proof. We have clarified this in a short treatise, which we named *al-Qawl al-Mufid fi Hukm al-Taqlid* ("The Beneficial Word on the Ruling on Taqlid").

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 21, verses 1–9 (part 2 of 2):

Then, when He, glory be to Him, had finished answering their doubt, He emphasized that the Messengers are of the same kind as human beings, and so He said: ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food﴾. That is, the Messengers are a model for the rest of the children of Adam in the judgment of nature: they eat as they eat and drink as they drink. "Jasad" (body) is the physical form of a human being. Al-Zajjaj said: it is singular, but it refers to a plurality, meaning "jasad" indicates a group; that is, "We did not make them possessors of bodies that do not eat food." Thus the clause ﴿that do not eat food﴾ is a description of "jasadan" (a body): that is, "We did not make them a body that is independent of eating, but rather it is in need of that." ﴿Nor were they immortal﴾, but they die as other human beings die, and they (the disbelievers) had believed that the Messengers do not die, so God answered them with this.

The clause ﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them﴾ is conjoined to a clause indicated by the context, and the implied sense is: "We revealed to them what We revealed, then We fulfilled the promise to them," that is, We carried out the promise We had made them of delivering them and destroying those who denied them. For this reason He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿So We delivered them and whom We willed﴾ of Our believing servants, and what is meant is their deliverance from the punishment, and the destruction of those who disbelieved by worldly punishment. By "the transgressors" (al-musrifin) is meant those who exceed the limit in disbelief and sins, and they are the polytheists.

Al-Nasa'i reported from Abu Sa'id, "from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning His saying: ﴿And they are heedless, turning away﴾, he said: 'In this world.'" Ibn Mardawayh reported from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the verse, he said: "From the affairs of this world." Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Qatadah concerning His saying: ﴿Nay, they say: a confusion of dreams﴾, that is, the act of dreams, and it is only a vision he saw; ﴿Nay, he has invented it; nay, he is a poet﴾, all of this was said by him; ﴿Let him bring us a sign as the first ones were sent﴾, as 'Isa and Musa brought clear proofs and messengers; ﴿No town We destroyed before them believed﴾, that is, when the Messengers came to their peoples with clear proofs and they did not believe, they were not given respite. Ibn Jarir reported from Qatadah, who said: "The people of Makkah said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'If what you say is true, and it would please you that we believe, then turn Safa into gold for us.' Then Jibril came to him and said: 'If you wish, it will be what your people asked, but if they then do not believe, they will not be given respite; and if you wish, you may give your people more time.' He said: 'Rather, I will give my people more time.' So God revealed: ﴿No town before them believed﴾," the verse.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food﴾, he says: We did not make them bodies that do not eat food; rather, We made them bodies that eat food.

Al-Bukhari and others narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Banu Isra'il, al-Kahf, Maryam and al-Anbiya' are among the first of the old (*'ataq*) surahs, and they are part of my ancient possessions (*tilad*)." Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu'aym, in *al-Hilya*, narrated from 'Amir ibn Rabi'a that a man from the Arabs stayed with him, and 'Amir honoured his lodging. 'Amir then spoke on the man's behalf to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The man came to 'Amir and said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a valley, and there is no valley among the Arabs better than it. I wanted to grant you a portion of it, to be yours and your descendants' after you." 'Amir said: "I have no need of your portion. A surah was revealed today that has made us forget the world: ﴿The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they are heedless, turning away﴾."

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Then, when He, glory be to Him, had finished answering their doubt, He emphasized that the Messengers are of the same kind as human beings, and so He said: ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food﴾. That is, the Messengers are a model for the rest of the children of Adam in the judgment of nature: they eat as they eat and drink as they drink. "Jasad" (body) is the physical form of a human being. Al-Zajjaj said: it is singular, but it refers to a plurality, meaning "jasad" indicates a group; that is, "We did not make them possessors of bodies that do not eat food." Thus the clause ﴿that do not eat food﴾ is a description of "jasadan" (a body): that is, "We did not make them a body that is independent of eating, but rather it is in need of that." ﴿Nor were they immortal﴾, but they die as other human beings die, and they (the disbelievers) had believed that the Messengers do not die, so God answered them with this.

The clause ﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them﴾ is conjoined to a clause indicated by the context, and the implied sense is: "We revealed to them what We revealed, then We fulfilled the promise to them," that is, We carried out the promise We had made them of delivering them and destroying those who denied them. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they are heedless, turning away.﴾ ﴿No fresh reminder comes to them from their Lord but they listen to it while playing.﴾ ﴿Their hearts are distracted. And the wrongdoers conspire in secret, saying, "Is this not but a human like you? Will you then go to magic while you see?"﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."﴾ ﴿But they said, "Confused dreams!" "Rather, he has invented it!" "Rather, he is a poet! Let him bring us a sign as the earlier messengers were sent."﴾ ﴿No town that We destroyed before them believed. Will they then believe?﴾ ﴿We did not send before you any but men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of the reminder, if you do not know.﴾ ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal.﴾ ﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them, and We saved them and whom We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors.﴾

The meaning of the reckoning's time drawing near is that it approaches them, because at every moment it is closer to them than the moment before. It is also said that everything that is coming is near, and the death of every person is the establishment of his hour; the Resurrection is also near in comparison with the time that has passed, since what remains of the world is less than what has passed. "The people" is general in meaning. It is also said that it refers to the polytheists in general, and it is said that it refers to the disbelievers of Makkah. On this view, it is said that "the reckoning" means their punishment on the Day of Badr. The clause ﴿while they are heedless, turning away﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (*hal*): that is, they are heedless of the world, turning away from the Hereafter, not preparing themselves with what is obligatory upon them of faith in Allah, observing His obligations, and refraining from His prohibitions.

The description of the reminder as *muhdath* ("fresh" or "newly created") has been used as evidence that the Qur'an is created (*muhdath*), since the reminder here is the Qur'an. It is answered that there is no dispute about the createdness of a composition made of sounds and letters, since it is renewed in its descent; so the meaning is that its sending down is newly created. The dispute is only about the inner speech (*al-kalam al-nafsi*). This question, namely the eternity or createdness of the Qur'an, afflicted many scholars and virtuous men in the era of the Ma'mun, the Mu'tasim and the Wathiq. What happened to Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal of severe beating and long imprisonment happened; and because of it, the neck of Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Khuza'i was struck, and a great trial arose at that time and after it. The story is too famous to be recounted. Whoever wishes to learn its truth should consult the biography of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal in *Siyar A'lam al-Nubala'* by the historian of Islam al-Dhahabi. They went further to declaring disbelief in whoever abstained (*waqf*). Would that they had not exceeded the limit of abstention and returning knowledge to the Knower of the unseen, for nothing of the kind of speech about this question was heard from the righteous predecessors, the Companions, the Successors and those after them, until the time of the trial and the appearance of this discussion. Nor was any word on it transmitted from them. Therefore, refraining from complying with what they called for, holding firmly to the skirts of abstention, and returning the knowledge of this to its Knower is the best course. In it is safety and freedom from declaring disbelief in groups of Allah's servants. The matter belongs to Allah, glorified is He.

His saying ﴿but they listen to it﴾ is a fully detached exception (*istithna' mufarragh*) in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause. The meaning is: no fresh reminder comes to them from their Lord at any state except that they listen to it along with play, mockery and the distraction of the hearts. It is said that it is in the nominative position as a substitute (*badal*) for the *waw* in *asarru*; this was said by al-Mubarrad and others. It is said that it is in the nominative position by way of vituperation (*dhamm*). It is said that it is the subject of an omitted verb, the implied meaning being "those who wronged said," and al-Nahhas preferred this. It is said that it is in the accusative position with the implied verb "I mean." It is said that it is in the genitive position as a substitute for *al-nas* ("the people"); al-Mubarrad mentioned this. It is said that it is in the nominative position as the subject of *asarru*, according to the dialect of those who permit two subjects together, like their saying *akalunī al-baraghīth* ("the fleas ate me"); al-Akhfash mentioned this. Similar to it is ﴿Then they were blind and deaf, many of them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 71]. From the same is the poet's saying:

*So the she-mules found their way to the targets.*

And the saying of another:

*But his father and mother drew near to me,*
*at Hawran, where his relatives press the pure oil.*

Al-Kisa'i said: there is inversion in it, that is: "And those who wronged conspired in secret." Abu 'Ubaydah said: *asarru* here is one of the words with opposite meanings: it may mean they concealed their speech, and it may mean they made it public and declared it. ﴿Is this not but a human like you?﴾ This sentence is with an implied "saying" before it: that is, they said, "Is this messenger not but a human like you, who is not distinguished from you by anything?" It is also permissible for this sentence to be a substitute for *al-najwa*, and *hal* here has the sense of negation: that is, and they conspired this talk in secret. The interrogative *hamza* in ﴿Will you then go to magic﴾ is for denunciation, and the *fa'* is for coordination with an implied element, as in its parallels. The clause ﴿while you see﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause. The meaning: if he is a human like you, and what he brought is magic, how can you respond to him and follow him? So Allah informed His Prophet (ﷺ) of what they whispered.

Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to answer them, and so He said: ﴿He said, "My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth"﴾, that is, nothing that is said in them is hidden from Him. In the codices of the people of Kufa it is "He said, *My Lord*," meaning Muhammad said, "My Lord knows the word, so He knows what you have conspired." It was said that the first reading is preferable, because they concealed this speech, so Allah informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of it and commanded him to say this to them. Al-Nahhas said: both readings are sound, and they are like two verses. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾: He hears everything that is heard and knows everything that is known, so this includes what they concealed, entering it at the first level. ﴿But they said, "Confused dreams!"﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: that is, they said that what he brings is confused dreams. Al-Qutaybi said: *adghath al-ahlam* are false visions. Al-Yazidi said: *al-adghath* are whatever has no interpretation. This is a turning away from Allah's side, glorified is He, relating what occurred from them, and a shift from relating their earlier saying to relating this statement. Then He, glorified is He, related their turning from their saying "confused dreams": He said, "Rather, he has invented it," that is, they said, "Rather, he has invented it on his own, with no basis." Then He, glorified is He, related that they turned from this and said, "Rather, he is a poet," and what he brought is of the kind of poetry. In this confusion, vacillation and indecision on their part is the greatest proof that they were ignorant of the reality of what he brought; they did not know what it was and did not recognize its nature. Or they knew that it was true and that it was from Allah, but they wanted to repel it with words and pelt it with every stone and clod, and this is the condition of one who has been overcome by proof and subdued by evidence. The position of the *kaf* is genitive as an adjective of *ayah* (sign). It is also permissible for it to be an adjective of an omitted verbal noun. Their request was a request of obstinacy, because Allah, glorified is He, had already given them signs sufficient for them. Had Allah known that they would believe if He gave them what they proposed, He would have given it to them, as He said: ﴿Had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear; and had He made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse﴾ [al-Anfal: 23]. Al-Zajjaj said: they proposed signs after which there would be no respite.

Then Allah answered them: ﴿No town that We destroyed before them believed﴾, that is, before the polytheists of Makkah. The meaning of *min qaryah* is "from the people of a town." He described the town by His saying *ahlaknaha*, that is, We destroyed its people, or We destroyed it by destroying its people. In this is an explanation that Allah's way with past nations was that when those who made proposals were given what they proposed and then did not believe, the punishment of annihilation descended upon them without doubt. It is said that it is in the nominative position as a substitute (*badal*) for the *waw* in *asarru*; this was said by al-Mubarrad and others. It is said that it is in the nominative position by way of vituperation (*dhamm*). It is said that it is the subject of an omitted verb, the implied meaning being "those who wronged said," and al-Nahhas preferred this. It is said that it is in the accusative position with the implied verb "I mean." It is said that it is in the genitive position as a substitute for *al-nas* ("the people"); al-Mubarrad mentioned this. It is said that it is in the nominative position as the subject of *asarru*, according to the dialect of those who permit two subjects together, like their saying *akalunī al-baraghīth* ("the fleas ate me"); al-Akhfash mentioned this. Similar to it is ﴿Then they were blind and deaf, many of them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 71]. From the same is the poet's saying:

*So the she-mules found their way to the targets.*

And the saying of another:

*But his father and mother drew near to me,*
*at Hawran, where his relatives press the pure oil.*

Al-Kisa'i said: there is inversion in it, that is: "And those who wronged conspired in secret." Abu 'Ubaydah said: *asarru* here is one of the words with opposite meanings: it may mean they concealed their speech, and it may mean they made it public and declared it. ﴿Is this not but a human like you?﴾ This sentence is with an implied "saying" before it: that is, they said, "Is this messenger not but a human like you, who is not distinguished from you by anything?" It is also permissible for this sentence to be a substitute for *al-najwa*, and *hal* here has the sense of negation: that is, and they conspired this talk in secret. The interrogative *hamza* in ﴿Will you then go to magic﴾ is for denunciation, and the *fa'* is for coordination with an implied element, as in its parallels. The clause ﴿while you see﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause. The meaning: if he is a human like you, and what he brought is magic, how can you respond to him and follow him? So Allah informed His Prophet (ﷺ) of what they whispered.

Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to answer them, and so He said: ﴿He said, "My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth"﴾, that is, nothing that is said in them is hidden from Him. In the codices of the people of Kufa it is "He said, *My Lord*," meaning Muhammad said, "My Lord knows the word, so He knows what you have conspired." It was said that the first reading is preferable, because they concealed this speech, so Allah informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of it and commanded him to say this to them. Al-Nahhas said: both readings are sound, and they are like two verses. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾: He hears everything that is heard and knows everything that is known, so this includes what they concealed, entering it at the first level. ﴿But they said, "Confused dreams!"﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: that is, they said that what he brings is confused dreams. Al-Qutaybi said: *adghath al-ahlam* are false visions. Al-Yazidi said: *al-adghath* are whatever has no interpretation. This is a turning away from Allah's side, glorified is He, relating what occurred from them, and a shift from relating their earlier saying to relating this statement. Then He, glorified is He, related their turning from their saying "confused dreams": He said, "Rather, he has invented it," that is, they said, "Rather, he has invented it on his own, with no basis." Then He, glorified is He, related that they turned from this and said, "Rather, he is a poet," and what he brought is of the kind of poetry. In this confusion, vacillation and indecision on their part is the greatest proof that they were ignorant of the reality of what he brought; they did not know what it was and did not recognize its nature. Or they knew that it was true and that it was from Allah, but they wanted to repel it with words and pelt it with every stone and clod, and this is the condition of one who has been overcome by proof and subdued by evidence. Then after all this, they said: ﴿Let him bring us a sign﴾; this is the answer to an omitted conditional: that is, if it is not as we have said, then let him bring us a sign ﴿as the earlier messengers were sent﴾, that is, as Musa was sent with the staff and other things, and Salih with the she-camel. The position of the *kaf* is genitive as an adjective of *ayah* (sign). It is also permissible for it to be an adjective of an omitted verbal noun. Their request was a request of obstinacy, because Allah, glorified is He, had already given them signs sufficient for them. Had Allah known that they would believe if He gave them what they proposed, He would have given it to them, as He said: ﴿Had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear; and had He made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse﴾ [al-Anfal: 23]. Al-Zajjaj said: they proposed signs after which there would be no respite.

Then Allah answered them: ﴿No town that We destroyed before them believed﴾, that is, before the polytheists of Makkah. The meaning of *min qaryah* is "from the people of a town." He described the town by His saying *ahlaknaha*, that is, We destroyed its people, or We destroyed it by destroying its people. In this is an explanation that Allah's way with past nations was that when those who made proposals were given what they proposed and then did not believe, the punishment of annihilation descended upon them without doubt. The *min* in *min qaryah* is superfluous, for emphasis. The meaning: no town of those towns which We destroyed, because of their proposals, believed before these people; so how would We give them what they propose, when they are the model of those before them? The interrogative *hamza* in ﴿Will they then believe?﴾ is for rebuke and reproach. The meaning: if a nation of the destroyed nations did not believe when given what they proposed, how would these people believe if they were given what they proposed?

Then He, glorified is He, answered their saying "Is this not but a human like you?" with His saying: ﴿We did not send before you any but men to whom We revealed﴾, that is, We did not send before you to the earlier nations except men from among mankind, and We did not send angels to them, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Say, "If there were angels walking calmly on the earth, We would have sent down upon them from the sky an angel as a messenger"﴾ [al-Isra': 95]. The clause ﴿to whom We revealed﴾ is a resumptive clause (*mustaanafah*) explaining the manner of sending, and it is also permissible for it to be an adjective of *rijalan*, that is, characterized by the attribute of revelation to them. Hafs, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *nuhi* with the *nun*, and the rest read it with the *ya'* (the lower dotted letter). Then Allah commanded them to ask the people of the reminder if they were ignorant of this, so He said: ﴿So ask the people of the reminder, if you do not know.﴾ The people of the reminder are the people of the two Scriptures: the Jews and the Christians. The meaning of ﴿if you do not know﴾ is: if you do not know that the messengers of Allah are human. So said most of the commentators. But the Jews and the Christians were not ignorant of this and did not deny it. The sense of the sentence is: if you do not know what has been mentioned, then ask the people of the reminder. The verse has been cited as evidence that *taqlid* (blind imitation) is permissible, and this is a mistake. Even if it were granted, the meaning would be asking them about the texts of the Book and the Sunnah, not about pure opinion. *Taqlid* is nothing but accepting the saying of another without his proof. We have clarified this in a short treatise, which we named *al-Qawl al-Mufid fi Hukm al-Taqlid* ("The Beneficial Word on the Ruling on Taqlid").

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 21, verses 1–9 (part 2 of 2):

Then, when He, glory be to Him, had finished answering their doubt, He emphasized that the Messengers are of the same kind as human beings, and so He said: ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food﴾. That is, the Messengers are a model for the rest of the children of Adam in the judgment of nature: they eat as they eat and drink as they drink. "Jasad" (body) is the physical form of a human being. Al-Zajjaj said: it is singular, but it refers to a plurality, meaning "jasad" indicates a group; that is, "We did not make them possessors of bodies that do not eat food." Thus the clause ﴿that do not eat food﴾ is a description of "jasadan" (a body): that is, "We did not make them a body that is independent of eating, but rather it is in need of that." ﴿Nor were they immortal﴾, but they die as other human beings die, and they (the disbelievers) had believed that the Messengers do not die, so God answered them with this.

The clause ﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them﴾ is conjoined to a clause indicated by the context, and the implied sense is: "We revealed to them what We revealed, then We fulfilled the promise to them," that is, We carried out the promise We had made them of delivering them and destroying those who denied them. For this reason He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿So We delivered them and whom We willed﴾ of Our believing servants, and what is meant is their deliverance from the punishment, and the destruction of those who disbelieved by worldly punishment. By "the transgressors" (al-musrifin) is meant those who exceed the limit in disbelief and sins, and they are the polytheists.

Al-Nasa'i reported from Abu Sa'id, "from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning His saying: ﴿And they are heedless, turning away﴾, he said: 'In this world.'" Ibn Mardawayh reported from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the verse, he said: "From the affairs of this world." Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Qatadah concerning His saying: ﴿Nay, they say: a confusion of dreams﴾, that is, the act of dreams, and it is only a vision he saw; ﴿Nay, he has invented it; nay, he is a poet﴾, all of this was said by him; ﴿Let him bring us a sign as the first ones were sent﴾, as 'Isa and Musa brought clear proofs and messengers; ﴿No town We destroyed before them believed﴾, that is, when the Messengers came to their peoples with clear proofs and they did not believe, they were not given respite. Ibn Jarir reported from Qatadah, who said: "The people of Makkah said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'If what you say is true, and it would please you that we believe, then turn Safa into gold for us.' Then Jibril came to him and said: 'If you wish, it will be what your people asked, but if they then do not believe, they will not be given respite; and if you wish, you may give your people more time.' He said: 'Rather, I will give my people more time.' So God revealed: ﴿No town before them believed﴾," the verse.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food﴾, he says: We did not make them bodies that do not eat food; rather, We made them bodies that eat food.

He drew His servants' attention to the greatness of His favor upon them by His saying: ﴿We have sent down to you a Book in which is your remembrance﴾, meaning the Qur'an. ﴿In which is your remembrance﴾ is a description of "a Book." The "remembrance" here means honor: that is, in it is your honor, as in His saying: ﴿And indeed it is a remembrance for you and for your people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44]. It was also said: "In it is your remembrance" means the mention of the matter of your religion, the rulings of your law, and what you will attain of reward or punishment. It was also said: "In it is your story." This was said by Mujahid. It was said: "In it are the noble qualities of your character and the excellence of your deeds." It was said: "In it is acting upon what your life depends on." This was said by Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah. It was said: "In it is your admonition." The interrogative in His saying ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ is for rebuke and reproach: that is, "Will you not reason that the matter is so?" or "Will you not reason about any of the things of which these are part?"

Then He threatened them and warned them of what befell the nations that denied, saying: ﴿And how many a town did We destroy, which had been wrongdoing﴾. The word "kam" (how many) is in the accusative position, as the object of "qasamna" (We destroyed). It is the informative "kam," which indicates multiplicity. Qasm means breaking and crushing something. It is said: "I broke the back of so-and-so" when you broke it, and "his tooth broke" when it was shattered. The meaning here is destruction and punishment. As for fasm with the letter fa', it means a split in a thing without separation. The clause ﴿which had been wrongdoing﴾ is in the genitive position as a description of "town." In the speech there is an omitted noun: that is, "And how many a town's people did We destroy, who were wrongdoers," meaning disbelievers in Allah, denying His signs. Wrongdoing (zulm) originally means placing a thing in other than its place, and they placed disbelief in the place of faith. ﴿And We brought into being after them another people﴾: that is, We created and produced, after the destruction of its people, a people who were not of them.

﴿So when they perceived Our might﴾: that is, they realized or saw Our punishment. Al-Akhfash said: they feared and anticipated it. Or "might" (ba's) means severe punishment. ﴿Behold, they were fleeing from it﴾. Rakd (fleeing) means running away, escaping and being routed. Its origin is from "rakada al-rajul al-dabbah" (the man spurred the mount with his legs). It is said "rakada al-faras" when he urged the horse on with his shanks. Then it became common until it was said "rakada al-faras" when it ran. From the same root is His saying: ﴿Strike with your foot﴾ [Sad: 42]. The meaning is that they fled from it, spurring their mounts. Then it was said to them: ﴿Do not flee﴾, that is, do not run away. It was said that the angels called out to them at the time of their flight. It was also said that those who said it to them were those present there from among the believers, mocking them and deriding them.

﴿And return to what you were made to enjoy of luxury and your dwellings﴾: that is, return to your blessings which were the cause of your insolence and disbelief. The mutraf is the one made to enjoy blessings; it is said "utrifa fulan," meaning he was given abundance in his livelihood. ﴿And your dwellings﴾: that is, return to your dwellings which you used to inhabit and boast of. ﴿Perhaps you will be questioned﴾: that is, you will be sought out to be asked and consulted and to plan regarding important matters. This is in the manner of mockery toward them and rebuke of them. It was also said: the meaning is "perhaps you will be asked about what punishment has befallen you, so you will inform about it." It was also said: "perhaps you will be asked to believe, as you used to be asked that before the punishment came upon you."

The commentators and the scholars of reports said: the intended people of this verse are the people of Hadur from Yemen. Allah, glorified is He, had sent to them a prophet named Shu'ayb ibn Muhaddam, whose grave is on one of the mountains of Yemen called Din, and between it and Hadur is about a postal distance. They said: he is not Shu'ayb, companion of Madyan. I say: the traces of the grave on the mountain of Din exist, and the common people of that region claim that it is the grave of Qudum ibn Qadim.

﴿They said: "O woe to us! Indeed we were wrongdoers."﴾ That is, when the angels said to them "Do not flee," they said: "O woe to us," that is, [they cried out] for our destruction: "Indeed we were wrongdoers," being wrongdoers to ourselves, deserving punishment for what we had sent forward. So they acknowledged against themselves the wrongdoing that necessitated punishment.

﴿And that remained their cry﴾: that is, this word remained their cry, meaning their call. The word is their saying "O woe to us!" That is, they called out with it and repeated it. ﴿Until We made them as cut stubble﴾: that is, with swords, as grain is harvested by the sickle. Hasid here means "mahsud" (reaped). The meaning of ﴿extinguished﴾ is that they were dead, from "khamadat al-nar" (the fire went out) when it was extinguished. So the extinction of life is compared to the extinction of fire, as it is said of one who has died: "he has been extinguished."

﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play﴾: that is, We did not create them in vain or for nothing, but to alert to the fact that they have a creator, capable, whose command must be obeyed. In this there is a general indication of the creation of the world. What is meant by "what is between them" is all the creatures existing between the heaven and the earth, despite the variety of their kinds and the diversity of their species.

﴿Had We wished to take a pastime﴾: lahw is what one amuses oneself with. It was said: lahw is wife and child; it was said: wife alone; it was said: child alone. Al-Jawhari said: lahw is sometimes used as a euphemism for intercourse. What he said is supported by the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

Did not Basbasah claim today that I have grown old and that people like me cannot enjoy pastime?

And from the same is the saying of another:

And among them is a pastime for the friend, and a sight.

The clause is a new sentence confirming the content of what precedes it. The answer to "law" (if) is His saying: ﴿We would have taken it from Ourselves﴾: that is, from Our presence and by Our power, not from yourselves. The commentators said: that is, from the Houris of paradise. In this there is a refutation of those who say that a wife and child are ascribed to Allah, exalted is He far above that with a great exaltation. It was also said: it intends to refute those who said: the idols or the angels are the daughters of Allah. Ibn Qutaybah said: the verse is a refutation of the Christians.

﴿If We were doing [it]﴾. Al-Wahidi said: the commentators said: "ma kunna fa'ilin" (we were not doing). Al-Farra', al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjaj said: it is permissible that "in" (if) is negative as the commentators mentioned: that is, We did not do that and did not take a wife or child. It is also permissible that it is conditional: that is, if We were of those who do that, We would have taken it from Ourselves. Al-Farra' said: this is the more likely of the two views according to the school of Arabic grammar.

﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it﴾. This is a turning away from the adoption of play: that is, leave that which they say, for it is a lie and falsehood. Rather, Our way is to hurl the truth upon falsehood, so it crushes it, that is, overpowers it. The origin of "damgh" is splitting the head until it reaches the brain, and from it comes "al-damigha" (the crushing calamity). Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that We remove it, removing it with the removal of humiliation and disgrace, since its origin is hitting the brain with a blow.

It was said: by "the truth" is meant the proof (hujjah). Ahh. And by "falsehood" their doubts. It was said: the truth is admonitions and falsehood is sins. It was said: falsehood is Satan. It was said: their lie and their describing Allah, glorified is He, with attributes not His.

﴿So then it is vanishing﴾: that is, it is departing and going away. It was said: it is perishing and destroyed. The meanings are close, and "idha" here is the sudden "idha" (then suddenly).

﴿And woe to you for what you describe﴾: that is, punishment in the Hereafter because of your describing Him with what is not befitting for Him. It was said: "woe" is a valley in Hell. It is a warning to Quraysh that for them is a punishment like that of those people. The "min" in "mimma" is causal (because of).

﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, as slaves and possession. He is their creator, their provider and their owner. How then could it be permissible for some of His creatures to be partners to Him, worshipped as He is worshipped? This sentence confirms what precedes it. ﴿And those near Him﴾ means the angels. In it is a refutation of those who say the angels are the daughters of Allah. In describing them as being near Him there is an indication of their honor and nobility, and that they are in the position of the close attendants of kings. Then He described them with His saying: ﴿They do not disdain to worship Him﴾: that is, they do not consider themselves too great nor refuse to worship Allah, glorified is He, and to humble themselves before Him. ﴿Nor do they grow weary﴾: that is, they do not tire. It is derived from "hasir," which is a camel that has stopped from exhaustion and fatigue. It is said: "hasara al-ba'ir yahsuru husuran" (the camel became exhausted and tired). "Istahsara" and "tahassara" are similar, and "hasartuhu" I made him weary, transitive and intransitive. Abu Zayd said: they do not tire. Ibn al-A'rabi said: they do not lose heart. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of the verse is that these whom you mentioned as children of Allah are the servants of Allah; they do not refuse His worship nor consider themselves too great for it, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord do not disdain His worship﴾ [al-A'raf: 206]. It was also said: the meaning is that they do not cease from His worship. These meanings are close.

﴿They glorify [Him] night and day; they do not slacken﴾: that is, they declare Allah free of imperfection, constantly, without weakening in that or growing tired. It was said: they pray night and day. Al-Zajjaj said: the course of glorification from them is like the course of breath from us; nothing distracts us from breathing, so their glorification is constant. This sentence is either a new sentence answering an implied question, or in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal).

﴿Or have they taken gods from the earth [who can] raise the dead?﴾ Al-Mufaddal said: the purpose of this interrogation is denial: that is, they have not taken gods able to give life. "Am" here is the disjunctive "am," and the hamza is for denying occurrence. Al-Mubarrad said: "am" here has the meaning of "hal" (is it that): that is, have these polytheists taken gods from the earth who give life to the dead? "Am" here cannot mean "bal" (rather), because that would imply that they can create the dead, unless "am" is taken as accompanied by an interrogative, making it the disjunctive "am," and then the meaning is sound. "Min al-ard" (from the earth) is connected to "ittakhadhu" (took), or to an omitted word which is a description of "gods." The meaning of "they raise" is they resurrect the dead. The clause is a description of "gods." This clause is what the denial and ignorance-attribution revolve around, not the taking itself, since that takes place from them without doubt. The meaning: "Rather, they have taken gods from the earth, [gods] who alone, despite their lowliness, raise the dead." But that is not the case, for those they took as gods are far from that. Al-Jumhur read "yunshirun" with a dammah on the ya' and a kasrah on the shin, from "anshara-hu," meaning "ahyahu" (gave him life). Al-Hasan read it with a fathah on the ya': that is, "yahyawna wa-la yamutun" (they live and do not die).

Then He, glorified is He, established proof of the invalidity of multiple gods, saying: ﴿Had there been within them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾: that is, had there been in the heavens and the earth gods worshipped other than Allah, they would have been ruined, meaning they would have been corrupted, namely the heavens and the earth with what is in them of creatures. Al-Kisa'i, Sibawayh, al-Akhfash, al-Zajjaj and the majority of grammarians said: "illa" here is not for exception but means "ghayr" (other than), a description of "gods." That is why the noun after it was in the nominative and the i'rab (grammatical inflection) of "ghayr" appeared in it, since "illa" here has the meaning of "ghayr." From it is the saying of the poet:

And every brother whose brother departs from him, by the life of your father, except the two Farqads [i.e., they do not depart].

Al-Farra' said: "illa" here means "siwa" (other than): the meaning being: had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined. The reason for ruin is that the existence of another god with Allah necessitates that each of them be capable of independent control of management, so conflict and disagreement occur, and corruption is caused by it. End.

﴿So glorified is Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe﴾. The "fa" (so) is to order what follows upon what precedes, from the establishment of oneness by proof: that is, He is exalted, mighty and majestic, above what is not befitting for Him, such as the existence of a partner for Him. In this is guidance for the servants to declare the Lord, glorified is He, free of what is not befitting for Him.

﴿He is not questioned about what He does﴾. This sentence is a new sentence explaining that He, glorified is He, because of the strength of His authority and the greatness of His majesty, is not asked by any of His creatures about any of His decree and destiny. ﴿But they will be questioned﴾, that is, the servants will be questioned about what they do; Allah will question them about that because they are His servants. It was also said: the meaning is that He, glorified is He, is not held accountable for His actions, while they are held accountable. It was said: the intended meaning is that He, glorified is He, made clear to His servants that whoever is questioned about his deeds, like the Messiah and the angels, is not suitable to be a god.
