Ibn Abi Shayba in *al-Musannaf*, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh related from him something similar, but longer. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also: *nafashat* means "grazed."

'Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ahmad, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, Ibn Maja, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh related from Haram ibn Muhayyisa: "A she-camel of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib entered a garden and damaged it. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) ruled that the owners of gardens are responsible for guarding them by day, and that what the livestock damages by night is the liability of their owners." This hadith has been criticised, and we have expanded the discussion on it in our commentary on *al-Muntaqa*. Ibn Mardawayh related a similar hadith from 'A'isha, and at its end he added: "Then he recited this verse: ﴿And Dawud and Sulayman﴾, [to the end of] the verse."

In the *Two Sahihs* and others, from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "While two women were with their two sons, a wolf came and took (p-945) one of the two. They brought their dispute to Dawud, and he ruled for the elder. They went out, and Sulayman called them and said: 'Bring me a knife, I will split it between you.' The younger said: 'May God have mercy on you, he is her son; do not split him.' So he ruled for the younger." Although this hadith is not included in what the verse narrates of their judgment, it is among the events that happened to them.

'Abd al-Razzaq, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh in *al-'Azama* related from Qatada, concerning His words: ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Us] with Dawud, and the birds﴾, he said: they prayed with Dawud when he prayed. ﴿And We taught him the making of armour for you﴾, he said: they were plates; the first to weave and link them was Dawud, peace be upon him.

Ibn Abi Shayba and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, related from Ibn 'Abbas: Sulayman would have six hundred thousand chairs set out for him. Then the nobles of mankind would come and sit nearest to him. Then the nobles of the jinn would come and sit next to the nobles of mankind. Then he would call the birds, and they would shade them. Then he would call the wind, and it would carry them, travelling a month's distance in a single morning.

Ibn 'Asakir, al-Daylami and Ibn al-Najjar related from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God said to Ayyub: 'Do you know what your offence against Me was, that I tested you?' He said: 'No, O Lord.' He said: 'Because you entered upon Pharaoh and flattered him in two words.'"

Ibn 'Asakir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Ayyub's sin was only that a poor man sought his help against an oppressor whom he could have repelled, but he did not help him, nor did he command the good, nor did he forbid the oppressor from oppressing the poor man, so God tested him. In its chain is Juwaybir.

Ibn Abi Shayba and Ahmad in *al-Zuhd*, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Nu'aym in *al-Hilya* related from 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, who said: Ayyub had two brothers who came one day, but they could not bear to draw near to him because of his smell, so they stood at a distance. One of them said to the other: "If God had known any good in Ayyub, He would not have tested him with this." Ayyub was distressed by their words with a distress greater than any he had ever felt. He said: "O God, if You know that I have never spent a night full while I knew where a hungry person was, then confirm me." He was confirmed from the sky while they were listening. Then he said: "O God, if You know that I have never worn a shirt while I knew where a naked person was, then confirm me." He was confirmed from the sky while they were listening. Then he fell prostrate and said: "O God, by Your might, I will not raise my head until You remove it from me." He did not raise his head until God removed it from him.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it through another chain, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And We gave him his family and the like of them with them﴾, that he said: It was said to him, "O Ayyub, your family is yours in Paradise. If you wish, We will bring them to you, and if you wish, We will leave them for you in Paradise." Rather, leave them for Me in Paradise, and in this world you will be given the like of them.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani narrated from al-Dahhak, who said: It reached Ibn Mas'ud that Marwan had said regarding this verse, ﴿And We gave him his family and the like of them with them﴾, "He was given a family other than his family." Ibn Mas'ud said: "Rather, he was given his family in their very persons, and the like of them with them."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Ruyani, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ayyub remained in his affliction for eighteen years. Near and distant people abandoned him, except for two men among his brothers who were among his closest brothers. They used to come to him in the morning and in the evening. One of them said to his companion one day: 'By Allah, you know Ayyub has committed a sin that no one else has committed.' He asked: 'What is that?' He said: 'For eighteen years Allah has not shown him mercy, so He has not removed what afflicts him.' When they went to Ayyub, the man could not restrain himself until he mentioned that to him. Ayyub said: 'I do not know what he is saying, except that Allah knows that I pass by two men quarrelling, mentioning Allah, so I return to my house and expiate for them, out of dislike that Allah should be mentioned except in what is right.' He used to go out for his need, and when he had finished, his wife would take hold of his hand until he reached [his place]. One day she was late with him, so Allah revealed to Ayyub, in his place, ﴿Strike with your foot; this is a cool bath and a drink﴾ [Sad: 42]. She was slow to come to him, so she met him while he was coming towards her, and Allah had removed from him the affliction that he had, and he was in his best condition. When she saw him she said: 'May Allah bless you! Have you seen the afflicted Prophet of Allah? By Allah, I have never seen a man more like him than you when he was healthy.' He said: 'I am he.'" He had two granaries: a granary for wheat and a granary for barley. Allah sent two clouds. When one of them was over the wheat granary, it poured gold into it until it overflowed, and the other poured silver into the barley granary until it overflowed.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding His words ﴿And Dhu al-Kifl﴾, that he said: "He was a righteous man, not a prophet, who undertook for the prophet of his people that he would take charge of their affairs for him, establish order among them, and judge between them with justice. He did so, and so he was named Dhu al-Kifl (the one of the guarantee)."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "There was a judge among the Children of Israel, and death came to him. He said: 'Who will take my place on the condition that he does not become angry?' A man said: 'I will.' So he was named Dhu al-Kifl." He mentioned the story. He would pray all night, then in the morning he would stand and judge between the people.

Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: "Dhu al-Kifl was not a prophet. Rather, among the Children of Israel there was a righteous man who prayed one hundred prayers every day. When he died, Dhu al-Kifl took on his responsibility after him, and he prayed one hundred prayers every day, so he was named Dhu al-Kifl."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it hasan (good), Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman narrated through the chain of Sa'd, the freed slave of Talhah, from Ibn Umar, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Al-Kifl from the Children of Israel did not refrain from any sin he committed. A woman came to him, and he gave her sixty dinars on condition that he would have intercourse with her. When he sat between her legs as a man sits with his wife, she trembled and wept. He said: 'What makes you weep? Have I forced you?' She said: 'No, but this is an act I have never done before, and only need drove me to it.' He said: 'You do this, and you have never done it? Go, it is yours.' He said: 'By Allah, I will never disobey Allah after this, ever.' He died that same night, and in the morning it was written on his door: 'Indeed, Allah has forgiven al-Kifl.'" al-Tirmidhi, who graded it hasan, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through the chain of Sa'd, the freed slave of Talhah.

(p. 946) Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the chain of Nafi', from Ibn Amr, who said: "In it [the verse] is Dhu al-Kifl."

Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿And Dhu al-Nun, when he went off in anger﴾, that he said: "He became angry with his people." ﴿And he thought that We would not have power over him﴾, meaning: that We would not decree a punishment or a trial upon him for what he did to his people in his anger toward them and his fleeing. He said: "His punishment was that the whale seized him."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿And he thought that We would not have power over him﴾, that he said: "He thought that the punishment that befell him would not seize him."

Ahmad in al-Zuhd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿And he called out in the darknesses﴾, that he said: "The darkness of the night, the darkness of the belly of the whale, and the darkness of the sea."

Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir al-Usul, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The supplication of Dhu al-Nun when he was in the belly of the whale: "There is no god but You, glory be to You, indeed I have been among the wrongdoers." No Muslim has ever called upon his Lord with it concerning anything except that He has responded to him.'"

Ibn Jarir narrated from him (Ibn Abbas) that he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The Name of Allah by which, when He is called upon, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives, is the supplication of Yunus ibn Matta.'" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this specific to Yunus, or to the whole community of Muslims?" He said: "It is specific to Yunus, and general for the believers when they call upon Him with it. Have you not heard the words of Allah: ﴿And thus We deliver the believers﴾? So it is a condition from Allah for whoever calls upon Him with it."

al-Hakim narrated a similar report from his (Ibn Abbas's) narration as well. It is established in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others, from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not proper for anyone to say: 'I am better than Yunus ibn Matta.'" It is also narrated in the Sahih and elsewhere from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, and it is also narrated in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 21, verses 89–97 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: "And Zakariyya" — that is, recall the account of Zakariyya (Zechariah) when he called upon his Lord, saying: ﴿My Lord, do not leave me alone (fardan)﴾ — that is, solitary and childless. The discussion of this verse has already passed in Al ʿImran: ﴿and You are the best of inheritors﴾ — that is, the best of those who remain after everyone who dies. So: You are sufficient for me if You do not grant me a son, for I know that You do not waste Your religion, and that someone from Your servants whom You choose and approve will carry it out for the purpose of conveyance (al-tabligh).

﴿So We answered him﴾ — his supplication — ﴿and We gave him Yahya (John)﴾. This has already been treated fully in Surah Maryam. ﴿And We set right for him his wife﴾. Most of the exegetes said: she had been barren, and Allah made her fertile; this is the meaning of "setting right his wife." It was also said: she had a bad character, and Allah made her good in character. There is no barrier to intending both matters together: Allah, glorified is He, sets right her person, so she becomes fertile after having been barren, and sets right her character, so her character becomes pleasing after having been displeasing.

The clause ﴿Indeed they used to hasten to good deeds﴾ serves as a reason for what precedes it, namely His kindness, glorified is He, toward His prophets, peace be upon them. The pronoun refers to them. It was also said that it refers to Zakariyya, his wife, and Yahya. Then Allah, glorified is He, described them as those who ﴿call upon Us with longing and fear﴾ — that is, they supplicate to Him in times of ease and in times of hardship. It was also said: "raghab" is raising the palms' inner surfaces toward the sky, and "rahab" is raising their backs. The accusative of "raghaban wa-rahaban" is either as a verbal noun (masdar): that is, they long with longing and fear with fear; or as a reason (ʿilla): that is, for longing and fear; or as a circumstantial state (hal): that is, longing and fearing. Talha ibn Musarrif read "wa-yadʿunana" with a single nun; al-Aʿmash read with a damma on the rāʾ in both words and sukun on what follows; Ibn Wathhab read with a fatha on the rāʾ in both words and a fatha on what follows in both. ﴿And they were humble before Us﴾ — that is, submissive and supplicating.

﴿And she who guarded her chastity (ahsanat farjaha)﴾ — that is, recall her account: she is Maryam (Mary). She guarded her chastity from both the lawful and the unlawful, and no human touched her. He mentioned her alongside the prophets, though she was not among them, because of the mention of ʿIsa (Jesus), and because of the wondrous sign in the account of her. ﴿So We breathed into her of Our Spirit﴾ — Allah, glorified is He, attributed the Spirit to Himself, as an honour and exaltation, and He means the Spirit of ʿIsa. ﴿And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the sign is singular in them, because she bore him without a male. It was also said: according to the view of Sibawayh, the sense is: "We made her a sign, and We made her son a sign," like His saying: ﴿And Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him﴾ [al-Tawba: 62]. The meaning is that Allah, glorified is He, made their account a complete sign, along with the abundance of signs in each of them. It was also said: by "sign" He meant the all-encompassing category, which includes the signs belonging to each of them. The meaning of "ahsanat" is that she was chaste, refrained from immorality and other things. It was also said: by "farj" is meant the collar of the garment, that is, her garments were pure. The explanation of similar matters has passed in Surah al-Nisa' and Maryam.

Then, when He mentioned the prophets, He made clear that they were all united upon monotheism, and said: ﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community (ummatan wahidatan)﴾. The word "ummah" means religion, as Ibn Qutayba said, and similarly ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a community (ummah)﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 22] — that is, upon a religion. It is as if He said: this, your religion, is one religion, with no disagreement among the differing nations regarding monotheism, and none departs from this except the unbelieving polytheists who associate others with Allah. It was also said: the meaning is that this law which I have explained to you in your Book is one law. It was also said: the meaning is that this your creed is one creed, namely the creed of Islam. The accusative of "ummatan wahidatan" is as a circumstantial state: that is, agreed, not differing. It was read "inna hadhihi ummatakum" with the accusative of "ummatakum" as an apposition (badal) to the subject of "inna," with the predicate "ummatun wahidatun." It was also read with the nominative of "ummatukum" and the nominative of "ummatun," as two predicates; and it was said that it is by supposing an implied subject, that is: it is one community. The majority read "ummatukum" in the nominative as the predicate, and "ummatan" in the accusative as a circumstantial state, as we have previously mentioned. Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: it is in the mode of a cut (al-qat') because an indefinite noun comes after the completion of the sentence. ﴿And I am your Lord, so worship Me﴾ — exclusively; do not worship other than Me, whatever it may be.

﴿And they cut their affair among themselves﴾ — that is, they split into sects in religion until they became like scattered pieces. Al-Akhfash said: they differed concerning it, and this is like the first statement. Al-Azhari said: that is, they dispersed in their affair, so "amrahum" is in the accusative by the omission of "fi" (in). The intended people in the verse are the polytheists, whom Allah censured for opposing the truth and taking gods besides Allah. It was also said: the intended meaning is all creation, and that they made their affair in their religions into pieces and divided it among themselves: this one is a monotheist, this one is a Jew, this one is a Christian, this one is a Magian, and this one is an idol-worshipper. Then Allah, glorified is He, informed that the return of all is to Him, saying: ﴿all of them to Us are returning﴾ — that is, each one of these sects is returning to Us for resurrection, not to anyone else.

﴿So whoever does of the righteous deeds﴾ — that is, whoever does some of the righteous deeds, not all of them, since no one can bear that — ﴿while he is a believer﴾ in Allah, His messengers, and the Last Day, ﴿his effort will not be denied﴾ — that is, there is no denial (judud) of his deed, and no wasting of its reward. Kufr is the opposite of iman, and kufr also means ingratitude for blessing, which is the opposite of shukr; it is said kafara kufuran wa-kufranan. In the reading of Ibn Masʿud: "fa-la kufra li-saʿyihi." ﴿And indeed, We are recording it for him﴾ — that is, We are preserving his effort. Similar to this is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, I do not waste the work of any worker among you, male or female﴾ [Al ʿImran: 195].

﴿And there is a prohibition upon a town which We have destroyed﴾. Zayd ibn Thabit and the people of Madina read "wa-haram," and the people of Kufa read "wa-haram" (with a different vowelling). The first reading was preferred by Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim, and the second reading was transmitted from ʿAli, Ibn Masʿud, and Ibn ʿAbbas; they are two dialects, like ḥill and ḥalal. Saʿid ibn Jubayr read "wa-harima" with a fatha on the ḥāʾ, a kasra on the rāʾ, and a fatha on the mīm. ʿIkrima and Abu al-ʿAliya read "ḥaruma" with a damma on the rāʾ and fatha on the ḥāʾ and mīm. The meaning of "ahlaknaha" is: We decreed its destruction. The clause ﴿that they do not return﴾ is in a position of nominative, either as a subject whose predicate is "ḥaram," or as an agent filling the place of its predicate. The meaning: it is absolutely impossible that they not return to Us for recompense. It was also said: "la" in "la yarji'un" is extra; that is: it is prohibited for a town which We have destroyed that they return to the world after destruction. Abu ʿUbayda chose this. It was also said: "ḥaram" here means "obligatory": that is, obligatory upon a town, and from this is the saying of al-Khansa':

And indeed, "ḥaram" — I do not see anyone weeping over his grief for the rest of time except that I wept over Sakhr.

It was also said: "ḥaram" means "impeded": their return to repentance is impossible, with "la" being extra. Al-Nahhas said: the verse is problematic, and among the best and most majestic things said about it is what Ibn ʿUyayna, Ibn ʿUlayya, Hushaym, Ibn Idris, Muhammad ibn Fadl, Sulaym ibn Hibban, and Mu'alla transmitted from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the meaning of the verse: he said: "it is decreed that they do not return," that is, they do not repent. Al-Zajjaj and Abu ʿAli al-Farisi said: there is an implied element in the speech, that is: "and it is prohibited upon a town for which We have decreed destruction, or the sealing of the hearts of its people, that any deed be accepted from them, because they do not return," that is, they do not repent.

﴿Until, when Yajuj and Majuj are let loose﴾. "Hatta" here is the one after which speech is related, with an omitted noun (al-mudaf). It was also said: this "hatta" is the one indicating a limit (li-l-ghaya). The meaning: those mentioned previously continue in what they are upon until the Day of Resurrection, which is the day of the opening of the barrier of Yajuj and Majuj. ﴿And they, from every elevation, will rush forth﴾ — the pronoun refers to Yajuj and Majuj. "Haddab" is every raised hill of the earth, and its plural is "ahdab," derived from the hump of the earth. The meaning of "yansilun" is "they hasten"; it was also said: "they come out." Al-Zajjaj said: "naslan" is the gait of a wolf when it hastens; one says nasala fulan fi al-ʿadw yansilu, with kasra and damma, nasl-an, nusul-an, and nuslan-an: that is, Yajuj and Majuj will hasten their pace from every elevated place on the earth and disperse across the earth. It was also said: the pronoun in "wa-hum" refers to all creation, and the meaning is that they will be gathered to the place of standing, hastening from every elevated place of the earth. It was read with a damma on the sīn. Al-Mahdawi transmitted this reading from Ibn Masʿud, and al-Tha'labi transmitted this reading as well from Mujahid and Abu al-Sahba'.

Al-Farra', al-Kisa'i, and others said: the intended "promise" is the true promise, the Resurrection, and the "wa" is extra; the meaning: until, when Yajuj and Majuj are opened, the true promise, which is the Resurrection, draws near; so "iqtarab" is the answer of "idha." Al-Farra' recited:

So when we passed the courtyard of the tribe and he set his course...

That is, "intaha." From this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And He threw him down upon his forehead﴾ and ﴿We called him﴾ [al-Saffat: 103–104]. Al-Farra' permitted that the answer of "idha" be ﴿then, behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring﴾. Al-Basriyyun said: the answer is omitted, and the estimate is: they will say, "O woe to us!"

Some have said the sentence is complete at His words *hiya*, and the implied construction is: *fa-idha hiya* (meaning) the Resurrection is *barizah* (manifest), *waqiʿah* (having occurred), as if it were *atiyah* (coming) and *hadirah* (present). Then he began and said: *shakhisah absar al-ladhina kafaru* (the eyes of those who disbelieved will be fixed in horror), placing the predicate before the subject, meaning: the eyes of those who disbelieved are fixed in horror. And *ya wayla-na* (woe to us), with an implied verb of saying, [means]: ﴿Indeed, you were in heedlessness of this﴾, that is, of this which has come upon us, of the Resurrection and the Reckoning. ﴿Rather, we were wrongdoers﴾: they retracted the description of themselves as heedless, meaning: we were not heedless, rather we were wrongdoers to ourselves by denying and by not submitting to the Messengers.

Al-Ḥākim narrated it and authenticated it from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words ﴿And We made his wife fit for him﴾, that he said: "The wife of Zakariyya had a problem in her tongue, and Allah rectified it." Something similar was narrated from a group of the Tabiʿun (Successors).

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding the verse, that he said: "We granted him her child."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, who said: "She was barren, so He made her fertile, and He granted him Yahya through her." Regarding His words ﴿And they were humbly submissive to Us﴾, he said: "Humbled."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Jurayj regarding His words ﴿And they called upon Us in hope and fear﴾, that he said: "Hope in the mercy of Allah and fear of the punishment of Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And they called upon Us in hope and fear﴾. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nuʿaym in *al-Hilyah*, al-Ḥākim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shuʿab* narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUkaym, who said: "Abu Bakr al-Siddiq addressed us, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'Amma baʿd (to proceed). I enjoin you to have taqwa of Allah, and to praise Him with what He is worthy of, and to mix hope with fear, for Allah praised Zakariyya and his family, saying: ﴿Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and call upon Us in hope and fear, and they were humbly submissive to Us﴾.'"

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community﴾, that he said: "Indeed, this is your religion, one religion." Ibn Jarir narrated the like of it from Mujahid. ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Qatadah.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Zayd regarding His words ﴿And they cut their affair among themselves into sects﴾, that he said: "*Taqqaʿu* means they differed regarding the religion."

Al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shuʿab* narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿And there is a prohibition upon a town which We have destroyed﴾, that he said: "It became obligatory to destroy it." ﴿That they will not return﴾: he said: "They will not repent."

Saʿid ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he used to recite (*wa-ḥarama ʿala qaryatin*, with a different verb form), and said: "It became obligatory upon a town ﴿which We destroyed that they will not return﴾," as He said: ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, that to them they do not return?﴾ [Yasin: 31].

ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated the like of it from ʿIkrimah and Saʿid ibn Jubayr.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿From every slope﴾, that he said: "A height (*sharaf*), they will swarm (*yansilun*)," and he said: "They will advance (*yuqbilun*)." Numerous hadiths have been transmitted concerning the description of Yajuj and Majuj and the time of their emergence, but mentioning them here is of little benefit.

The pronoun refers to them. It was also said that it refers to Zakariyya, his wife, and Yahya. Then Allah, glorified is He, described them as those who ﴿call upon Us with longing and fear﴾ — that is, they supplicate to Him in times of ease and in times of hardship. It was also said: "raghab" is raising the palms' inner surfaces toward the sky, and "rahab" is raising their backs. Talha ibn Musarrif read "wa-yadʿunana" with a single nun; al-Aʿmash read with a damma on the rāʾ in both words and sukun on what follows; Ibn Wathhab read with a fatha on the rāʾ in both words and a fatha on what follows in both. ﴿And they were humble before Us﴾ — that is, submissive and supplicating.

﴿And she who guarded her chastity (ahsanat farjaha)﴾ — that is, recall her account: she is Maryam (Mary). She guarded her chastity from both the lawful and the unlawful, and no human touched her. He mentioned her alongside the prophets, though she was not among them, because of the mention of ʿIsa (Jesus), and because of the wondrous sign in the account of her. ﴿So We breathed into her of Our Spirit﴾ — Allah, glorified is He, attributed the Spirit to Himself, as an honour and exaltation, and He means the Spirit of ʿIsa. ﴿And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the sign is singular in them, because she bore him without a male. The meaning is that Allah, glorified is He, made their account a complete sign, along with the abundance of signs in each of them. It was also said: by "sign" He meant the all-encompassing category, which includes the signs belonging to each of them. The meaning of "ahsanat" is that she was chaste, refrained from immorality and other things. It was also said: by "farj" is meant the collar of the garment, that is, her garments were pure. The explanation of similar matters has passed in Surah al-Nisa' and Maryam.

The accusative of "ummatan wahidatan" is as a circumstantial state: that is, agreed, not differing. It was read "inna hadhihi ummatakum" with the accusative of "ummatakum" as an apposition (badal) to the subject of "inna," with the predicate "ummatun wahidatun." It was also read with the nominative of "ummatukum" and the nominative of "ummatun," as two predicates; and it was said that it is by supposing an implied subject, that is: it is one community. Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: it is in the mode of a cut (al-qat') because an indefinite noun comes after the completion of the sentence. ﴿And I am your Lord, so worship Me﴾ — exclusively; do not worship other than Me, whatever it may be.

Al-Akhfash said: they differed concerning it, and this is like the first statement. Al-Azhari said: that is, they dispersed in their affair, so "amrahum" is in the accusative by the omission of "fi" (in). The intended people in the verse are the polytheists, whom Allah censured for opposing the truth and taking gods besides Allah. It was also said: the intended meaning is all creation, and that they made their affair in their religions into pieces and divided it among themselves: this one is a monotheist, this one is a Jew, this one is a Christian, this one is a Magian, and this one is an idol-worshipper. Kufr is the opposite of iman, and kufr also means ingratitude for blessing, which is the opposite of shukr; it is said kafara kufuran wa-kufranan. In the reading of Ibn Masʿud: "fa-la kufra li-saʿyihi." ﴿And indeed, We are recording it for him﴾ — that is, We are preserving his effort. Similar to this is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, I do not waste the work of any worker among you, male or female﴾ [Al ʿImran: 195].

The pronoun refers to them. It was also said that it refers to Zakariyya, his wife, and Yahya. Then Allah, glorified is He, described them as those who ﴿call upon Us with longing and fear﴾ — that is, they supplicate to Him in times of ease and in times of hardship. It was also said: "raghab" is raising the palms' inner surfaces toward the sky, and "rahab" is raising their backs. The accusative of "raghaban wa-rahaban" is either as a verbal noun (masdar): that is, they long with longing and fear with fear; or as a reason (ʿilla): that is, for longing and fear; or as a circumstantial state (hal): that is, longing and fearing. Talha ibn Musarrif read "wa-yadʿunana" with a single nun; al-Aʿmash read with a damma on the rāʾ in both words and sukun on what follows; Ibn Wathhab read with a fatha on the rāʾ in both words and a fatha on what follows in both. ﴿And they were humble before Us﴾ — that is, submissive and supplicating.

﴿And she who guarded her chastity (ahsanat farjaha)﴾ — that is, recall her account: she is Maryam (Mary). She guarded her chastity from both the lawful and the unlawful, and no human touched her. He mentioned her alongside the prophets, though she was not among them, because of the mention of ʿIsa (Jesus), and because of the wondrous sign in the account of her. ﴿So We breathed into her of Our Spirit﴾ — Allah, glorified is He, attributed the Spirit to Himself, as an honour and exaltation, and He means the Spirit of ʿIsa. ﴿And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the sign is singular in them, because she bore him without a male. It was also said: according to the view of Sibawayh, the sense is: "We made her a sign, and We made her son a sign," like His saying: ﴿And Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him﴾ [al-Tawba: 62]. The meaning is that Allah, glorified is He, made their account a complete sign, along with the abundance of signs in each of them. It was also said: by "sign" He meant the all-encompassing category, which includes the signs belonging to each of them. The meaning of "ahsanat" is that she was chaste, refrained from immorality and other things. It was also said: by "farj" is meant the collar of the garment, that is, her garments were pure. The explanation of similar matters has passed in Surah al-Nisa' and Maryam.

Then, when He mentioned the prophets, He made clear that they were all united upon monotheism, and said: ﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community (ummatan wahidatan)﴾. The word "ummah" means religion, as Ibn Qutayba said, and similarly ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a community (ummah)﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 22] — that is, upon a religion. It is as if He said: this, your religion, is one religion, with no disagreement among the differing nations regarding monotheism, and none departs from this except the unbelieving polytheists who associate others with Allah. It was also said: the meaning is that this law which I have explained to you in your Book is one law. It was also said: the meaning is that this your creed is one creed, namely the creed of Islam. The accusative of "ummatan wahidatan" is as a circumstantial state: that is, agreed, not differing. It was read "inna hadhihi ummatakum" with the accusative of "ummatakum" as an apposition (badal) to the subject of "inna," with the predicate "ummatun wahidatun." It was also read with the nominative of "ummatukum" and the nominative of "ummatun," as two predicates; and it was said that it is by supposing an implied subject, that is: it is one community. The majority read "ummatukum" in the nominative as the predicate, and "ummatan" in the accusative as a circumstantial state, as we have previously mentioned. Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: it is in the mode of a cut (al-qat') because an indefinite noun comes after the completion of the sentence. ﴿And I am your Lord, so worship Me﴾ — exclusively; do not worship other than Me, whatever it may be.

﴿And they cut their affair among themselves﴾ — that is, they split into sects in religion until they became like scattered pieces. Al-Akhfash said: they differed concerning it, and this is like the first statement. Al-Azhari said: that is, they dispersed in their affair, so "amrahum" is in the accusative by the omission of "fi" (in). The intended people in the verse are the polytheists, whom Allah censured for opposing the truth and taking gods besides Allah. It was also said: the intended meaning is all creation, and that they made their affair in their religions into pieces and divided it among themselves: this one is a monotheist, this one is a Jew, this one is a Christian, this one is a Magian, and this one is an idol-worshipper. Then Allah, glorified is He, informed that the return of all is to Him, saying: ﴿all of them to Us are returning﴾ — that is, each one of these sects is returning to Us for resurrection, not to anyone else.

﴿So whoever does of the righteous deeds﴾ — that is, whoever does some of the righteous deeds, not all of them, since no one can bear that — ﴿while he is a believer﴾ in Allah, His messengers, and the Last Day, ﴿his effort will not be denied﴾ — that is, there is no denial (judud) of his deed, and no wasting of its reward. Kufr is the opposite of iman, and kufr also means ingratitude for blessing, which is the opposite of shukr; it is said kafara kufuran wa-kufranan. In the reading of Ibn Masʿud: "fa-la kufra li-saʿyihi." ﴿And indeed, We are recording it for him﴾ — that is, We are preserving his effort. Similar to this is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, I do not waste the work of any worker among you, male or female﴾ [Al ʿImran: 195].

﴿And there is a prohibition upon a town which We have destroyed﴾. Zayd ibn Thabit and the people of Madina read "wa-haram," and the people of Kufa read "wa-haram" (with a different vowelling). The first reading was preferred by Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim, and the second reading was transmitted from ʿAli, Ibn Masʿud, and Ibn ʿAbbas; they are two dialects, like ḥill and ḥalal. Saʿid ibn Jubayr read "wa-harima" with a fatha on the ḥāʾ, a kasra on the rāʾ, and a fatha on the mīm. ʿIkrima and Abu al-ʿAliya read "ḥaruma" with a damma on the rāʾ and fatha on the ḥāʾ and mīm. The meaning of "ahlaknaha" is: We decreed its destruction. The clause ﴿that they do not return﴾ is in a position of nominative, either as a subject whose predicate is "ḥaram," or as an agent filling the place of its predicate. The meaning: it is absolutely impossible that they not return to Us for recompense. It was also said: "la" in "la yarji'un" is extra; that is: it is prohibited for a town which We have destroyed that they return to the world after destruction. Abu ʿUbayda chose this. It was also said: "ḥaram" here means "obligatory": that is, obligatory upon a town, and from this is the saying of al-Khansa':

And indeed, "ḥaram" — I do not see anyone weeping over his grief for the rest of time except that I wept over Sakhr.

It was also said: "ḥaram" means "impeded": their return to repentance is impossible, with "la" being extra. Al-Nahhas said: the verse is problematic, and among the best and most majestic things said about it is what Ibn ʿUyayna, Ibn ʿUlayya, Hushaym, Ibn Idris, Muhammad ibn Fadl, Sulaym ibn Hibban, and Mu'alla transmitted from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the meaning of the verse: he said: "it is decreed that they do not return," that is, they do not repent. Al-Zajjaj and Abu ʿAli al-Farisi said: there is an implied element in the speech, that is: "and it is prohibited upon a town for which We have decreed destruction, or the sealing of the hearts of its people, that any deed be accepted from them, because they do not return," that is, they do not repent.

﴿Until, when Yajuj and Majuj are let loose﴾. "Hatta" here is the one after which speech is related, with an omitted noun (al-mudaf). It was also said: this "hatta" is the one indicating a limit (li-l-ghaya). The meaning: those mentioned previously continue in what they are upon until the Day of Resurrection, which is the day of the opening of the barrier of Yajuj and Majuj. ﴿And they, from every elevation, will rush forth﴾ — the pronoun refers to Yajuj and Majuj. "Haddab" is every raised hill of the earth, and its plural is "ahdab," derived from the hump of the earth. The meaning of "yansilun" is "they hasten"; it was also said: "they come out." Al-Zajjaj said: "naslan" is the gait of a wolf when it hastens; one says nasala fulan fi al-ʿadw yansilu, with kasra and damma, nasl-an, nusul-an, and nuslan-an: that is, Yajuj and Majuj will hasten their pace from every elevated place on the earth and disperse across the earth. It was also said: the pronoun in "wa-hum" refers to all creation, and the meaning is that they will be gathered to the place of standing, hastening from every elevated place of the earth. It was read with a damma on the sīn. Al-Mahdawi transmitted this reading from Ibn Masʿud, and al-Tha'labi transmitted this reading as well from Mujahid and Abu al-Sahba'.

﴿And the promise draws near﴾ — it is coordinated (ʿatf) upon "futihat," and what is meant is the reckoning that follows the opening. Al-Farra', al-Kisa'i, and others said: the intended "promise" is the true promise, the Resurrection, and the "wa" is extra; the meaning: until, when Yajuj and Majuj are opened, the true promise, which is the Resurrection, draws near; so "iqtarab" is the answer of "idha." Al-Farra' recited:

So when we passed the courtyard of the tribe and he set his course...

That is, "intaha." From this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And He threw him down upon his forehead﴾ and ﴿We called him﴾ [al-Saffat: 103–104]. Al-Farra' permitted that the answer of "idha" be ﴿then, behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring﴾. Al-Basriyyun said: the answer is omitted, and the estimate is: they will say, "O woe to us!"

The Dhamir in *fa-idha hiya* refers to the story (*al-qissah*), or it is an ambiguous pronoun explained by what follows. *Idha* is used for sudden occurrence (*li-l-mufajaʾah*). Some have said the sentence is complete at His words *hiya*, and the implied construction is: *fa-idha hiya* (meaning) the Resurrection is *barizah* (manifest), *waqiʿah* (having occurred), as if it were *atiyah* (coming) and *hadirah* (present). Then he began and said: *shakhisah absar al-ladhina kafaru* (the eyes of those who disbelieved will be fixed in horror), placing the predicate before the subject, meaning: the eyes of those who disbelieved are fixed in horror. And *ya wayla-na* (woe to us), with an implied verb of saying, [means]: ﴿Indeed, you were in heedlessness of this﴾, that is, of this which has come upon us, of the Resurrection and the Reckoning. ﴿Rather, we were wrongdoers﴾: they retracted the description of themselves as heedless, meaning: we were not heedless, rather we were wrongdoers to ourselves by denying and by not submitting to the Messengers.

Al-Ḥākim narrated it and authenticated it from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words ﴿And We made his wife fit for him﴾, that he said: "The wife of Zakariyya had a problem in her tongue, and Allah rectified it." Something similar was narrated from a group of the Tabiʿun (Successors).

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding the verse, that he said: "We granted him her child."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, who said: "She was barren, so He made her fertile, and He granted him Yahya through her." Regarding His words ﴿And they were humbly submissive to Us﴾, he said: "Humbled."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Jurayj regarding His words ﴿And they called upon Us in hope and fear﴾, that he said: "Hope in the mercy of Allah and fear of the punishment of Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And they called upon Us in hope and fear﴾. He said: 'Hope, like this, and fear, like this,' and he spread his palms, meaning he placed their backs toward the ground in hope and reversed it in fear."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nuʿaym in *al-Hilyah*, al-Ḥākim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shuʿab* narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUkaym, who said: "Abu Bakr al-Siddiq addressed us, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'Amma baʿd (to proceed). I enjoin you to have taqwa of Allah, and to praise Him with what He is worthy of, and to mix hope with fear, for Allah praised Zakariyya and his family, saying: ﴿Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and call upon Us in hope and fear, and they were humbly submissive to Us﴾.'"

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community﴾, that he said: "Indeed, this is your religion, one religion." Ibn Jarir narrated the like of it from Mujahid. ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Qatadah.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Zayd regarding His words ﴿And they cut their affair among themselves into sects﴾, that he said: "*Taqqaʿu* means they differed regarding the religion."

Al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shuʿab* narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿And there is a prohibition upon a town which We have destroyed﴾, that he said: "It became obligatory to destroy it." ﴿That they will not return﴾: he said: "They will not repent."

Saʿid ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he used to recite (*wa-ḥarama ʿala qaryatin*, with a different verb form), and said: "It became obligatory upon a town ﴿which We destroyed that they will not return﴾," as He said: ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, that to them they do not return?﴾ [Yasin: 31].

ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated the like of it from ʿIkrimah and Saʿid ibn Jubayr.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿From every slope﴾, that he said: "A height (*sharaf*), they will swarm (*yansilun*)," and he said: "They will advance (*yuqbilun*)." Numerous hadiths have been transmitted concerning the description of Yajuj and Majuj and the time of their emergence, but mentioning them here is of little benefit.

The discussion of this verse has already passed in Al ʿImran: ﴿and You are the best of inheritors﴾ — that is, the best of those who remain after everyone who dies. There is no barrier to intending both matters together: Allah, glorified is He, sets right her person, so she becomes fertile after having been barren, and sets right her character, so her character becomes pleasing after having been displeasing.

The clause ﴿Indeed they used to hasten to good deeds﴾ serves as a reason for what precedes it, namely His kindness, glorified is He, toward His prophets, peace be upon them. The pronoun refers to them. It was also said that it refers to Zakariyya, his wife, and Yahya. Then he began and said: *shakhisah absar al-ladhina kafaru* (the eyes of those who disbelieved will be fixed in horror), placing the predicate before the subject, meaning: the eyes of those who disbelieved are fixed in horror. And *ya wayla-na* (woe to us), with an implied verb of saying, [means]: ﴿Indeed, you were in heedlessness of this﴾, that is, of this which has come upon us, of the Resurrection and the Reckoning. ﴿Rather, we were wrongdoers﴾: they retracted the description of themselves as heedless, meaning: we were not heedless, rather we were wrongdoers to ourselves by denying and by not submitting to the Messengers.

Al-Ḥākim narrated it and authenticated it from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words ﴿And We made his wife fit for him﴾, that he said: "The wife of Zakariyya had a problem in her tongue, and Allah rectified it." Something similar was narrated from a group of the Tabiʿun (Successors).

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding the verse, that he said: "We granted him her child."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, who said: "She was barren, so He made her fertile, and He granted him Yahya through her." Regarding His words ﴿And they were humbly submissive to Us﴾, he said: "Humbled."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Jurayj regarding His words ﴿And they called upon Us in hope and fear﴾, that he said: "Hope in the mercy of Allah and fear of the punishment of Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And they called upon Us in hope and fear﴾. He said: 'Hope, like this, and fear, like this,' and he spread his palms, meaning he placed their backs toward the ground in hope and reversed it in fear."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nuʿaym in *al-Hilyah*, al-Ḥākim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shuʿab* narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUkaym, who said: "Abu Bakr al-Siddiq addressed us, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'Amma baʿd (to proceed). I enjoin you to have taqwa of Allah, and to praise Him with what He is worthy of, and to mix hope with fear, for Allah praised Zakariyya and his family, saying: ﴿Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and call upon Us in hope and fear, and they were humbly submissive to Us﴾.'"

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community﴾, that he said: "Indeed, this is your religion, one religion." Ibn Jarir narrated the like of it from Mujahid. ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Qatadah.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Zayd regarding His words ﴿And they cut their affair among themselves into sects﴾, that he said: "*Taqqaʿu* means they differed regarding the religion."

Al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shuʿab* narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿And there is a prohibition upon a town which We have destroyed﴾, that he said: "It became obligatory to destroy it." ﴿That they will not return﴾: he said: "They will not repent."

Saʿid ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he used to recite (*wa-ḥarama ʿala qaryatin*, with a different verb form), and said: "It became obligatory upon a town ﴿which We destroyed that they will not return﴾," as He said: ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, that to them they do not return?﴾ [Yasin: 31].

ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated the like of it from ʿIkrimah and Saʿid ibn Jubayr.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿From every slope﴾, that he said: "A height (*sharaf*), they will swarm (*yansilun*)," and he said: "They will advance (*yuqbilun*)." Numerous hadiths have been transmitted concerning the description of Yajuj and Majuj and the time of their emergence, but mentioning them here is of little benefit.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 21, verses 89–97 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: "And Zakariyya" — that is, recall the account of Zakariyya (Zechariah) when he called upon his Lord, saying: ﴿My Lord, do not leave me alone (fardan)﴾ — that is, solitary and childless. The discussion of this verse has already passed in Al ʿImran: ﴿and You are the best of inheritors﴾ — that is, the best of those who remain after everyone who dies. So: You are sufficient for me if You do not grant me a son, for I know that You do not waste Your religion, and that someone from Your servants whom You choose and approve will carry it out for the purpose of conveyance (al-tabligh).

﴿So We answered him﴾ — his supplication — ﴿and We gave him Yahya (John)﴾. This has already been treated fully in Surah Maryam. ﴿And We set right for him his wife﴾. Most of the exegetes said: she had been barren, and Allah made her fertile; this is the meaning of "setting right his wife." It was also said: she had a bad character, and Allah made her good in character. There is no barrier to intending both matters together: Allah, glorified is He, sets right her person, so she becomes fertile after having been barren, and sets right her character, so her character becomes pleasing after having been displeasing.

The clause ﴿Indeed they used to hasten to good deeds﴾ serves as a reason for what precedes it, namely His kindness, glorified is He, toward His prophets, peace be upon them. The pronoun refers to them. It was also said that it refers to Zakariyya, his wife, and Yahya. Then Allah, glorified is He, described them as those who ﴿call upon Us with longing and fear﴾ — that is, they supplicate to Him in times of ease and in times of hardship. It was also said: "raghab" is raising the palms' inner surfaces toward the sky, and "rahab" is raising their backs. The accusative of "raghaban wa-rahaban" is either as a verbal noun (masdar): that is, they long with longing and fear with fear; or as a reason (ʿilla): that is, for longing and fear; or as a circumstantial state (hal): that is, longing and fearing. Talha ibn Musarrif read "wa-yadʿunana" with a single nun; al-Aʿmash read with a damma on the rāʾ in both words and sukun on what follows; Ibn Wathhab read with a fatha on the rāʾ in both words and a fatha on what follows in both. ﴿And they were humble before Us﴾ — that is, submissive and supplicating.

﴿And she who guarded her chastity (ahsanat farjaha)﴾ — that is, recall her account: she is Maryam (Mary). She guarded her chastity from both the lawful and the unlawful, and no human touched her. He mentioned her alongside the prophets, though she was not among them, because of the mention of ʿIsa (Jesus), and because of the wondrous sign in the account of her. ﴿So We breathed into her of Our Spirit﴾ — Allah, glorified is He, attributed the Spirit to Himself, as an honour and exaltation, and He means the Spirit of ʿIsa. ﴿And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the sign is singular in them, because she bore him without a male. It was also said: according to the view of Sibawayh, the sense is: "We made her a sign, and We made her son a sign," like His saying: ﴿And Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him﴾ [al-Tawba: 62]. The meaning is that Allah, glorified is He, made their account a complete sign, along with the abundance of signs in each of them. It was also said: by "sign" He meant the all-encompassing category, which includes the signs belonging to each of them. The meaning of "ahsanat" is that she was chaste, refrained from immorality and other things. It was also said: by "farj" is meant the collar of the garment, that is, her garments were pure. The explanation of similar matters has passed in Surah al-Nisa' and Maryam.

Then, when He mentioned the prophets, He made clear that they were all united upon monotheism, and said: ﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community (ummatan wahidatan)﴾. The word "ummah" means religion, as Ibn Qutayba said, and similarly ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a community (ummah)﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 22] — that is, upon a religion. It is as if He said: this, your religion, is one religion, with no disagreement among the differing nations regarding monotheism, and none departs from this except the unbelieving polytheists who associate others with Allah. It was also said: the meaning is that this law which I have explained to you in your Book is one law. It was also said: the meaning is that this your creed is one creed, namely the creed of Islam. The accusative of "ummatan wahidatan" is as a circumstantial state: that is, agreed, not differing. It was read "inna hadhihi ummatakum" with the accusative of "ummatakum" as an apposition (badal) to the subject of "inna," with the predicate "ummatun wahidatun." It was also read with the nominative of "ummatukum" and the nominative of "ummatun," as two predicates; and it was said that it is by supposing an implied subject, that is: it is one community. The majority read "ummatukum" in the nominative as the predicate, and "ummatan" in the accusative as a circumstantial state, as we have previously mentioned. Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: it is in the mode of a cut (al-qat') because an indefinite noun comes after the completion of the sentence. ﴿And I am your Lord, so worship Me﴾ — exclusively; do not worship other than Me, whatever it may be.

﴿And they cut their affair among themselves﴾ — that is, they split into sects in religion until they became like scattered pieces. Al-Akhfash said: they differed concerning it, and this is like the first statement. Al-Azhari said: that is, they dispersed in their affair, so "amrahum" is in the accusative by the omission of "fi" (in). The intended people in the verse are the polytheists, whom Allah censured for opposing the truth and taking gods besides Allah. It was also said: the intended meaning is all creation, and that they made their affair in their religions into pieces and divided it among themselves: this one is a monotheist, this one is a Jew, this one is a Christian, this one is a Magian, and this one is an idol-worshipper. Then Allah, glorified is He, informed that the return of all is to Him, saying: ﴿all of them to Us are returning﴾ — that is, each one of these sects is returning to Us for resurrection, not to anyone else.

﴿So whoever does of the righteous deeds﴾ — that is, whoever does some of the righteous deeds, not all of them, since no one can bear that — ﴿while he is a believer﴾ in Allah, His messengers, and the Last Day, ﴿his effort will not be denied﴾ — that is, there is no denial (judud) of his deed, and no wasting of its reward. Kufr is the opposite of iman, and kufr also means ingratitude for blessing, which is the opposite of shukr; it is said kafara kufuran wa-kufranan. In the reading of Ibn Masʿud: "fa-la kufra li-saʿyihi." ﴿And indeed, We are recording it for him﴾ — that is, We are preserving his effort. Similar to this is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, I do not waste the work of any worker among you, male or female﴾ [Al ʿImran: 195].

﴿And there is a prohibition upon a town which We have destroyed﴾. Zayd ibn Thabit and the people of Madina read "wa-haram," and the people of Kufa read "wa-haram" (with a different vowelling). The first reading was preferred by Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim, and the second reading was transmitted from ʿAli, Ibn Masʿud, and Ibn ʿAbbas; they are two dialects, like ḥill and ḥalal. Saʿid ibn Jubayr read "wa-harima" with a fatha on the ḥāʾ, a kasra on the rāʾ, and a fatha on the mīm. ʿIkrima and Abu al-ʿAliya read "ḥaruma" with a damma on the rāʾ and fatha on the ḥāʾ and mīm. The meaning of "ahlaknaha" is: We decreed its destruction. The clause ﴿that they do not return﴾ is in a position of nominative, either as a subject whose predicate is "ḥaram," or as an agent filling the place of its predicate. The meaning: it is absolutely impossible that they not return to Us for recompense. It was also said: "la" in "la yarji'un" is extra; that is: it is prohibited for a town which We have destroyed that they return to the world after destruction. Abu ʿUbayda chose this. It was also said: "ḥaram" here means "obligatory": that is, obligatory upon a town, and from this is the saying of al-Khansa':

And indeed, "ḥaram" — I do not see anyone weeping over his grief for the rest of time except that I wept over Sakhr.

It was also said: "ḥaram" means "impeded": their return to repentance is impossible, with "la" being extra. Al-Nahhas said: the verse is problematic, and among the best and most majestic things said about it is what Ibn ʿUyayna, Ibn ʿUlayya, Hushaym, Ibn Idris, Muhammad ibn Fadl, Sulaym ibn Hibban, and Mu'alla transmitted from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the meaning of the verse: he said: "it is decreed that they do not return," that is, they do not repent. Al-Zajjaj and Abu ʿAli al-Farisi said: there is an implied element in the speech, that is: "and it is prohibited upon a town for which We have decreed destruction, or the sealing of the hearts of its people, that any deed be accepted from them, because they do not return," that is, they do not repent.

﴿Until, when Yajuj and Majuj are let loose﴾. "Hatta" here is the one after which speech is related, with an omitted noun (al-mudaf). It was also said: this "hatta" is the one indicating a limit (li-l-ghaya). The meaning: those mentioned previously continue in what they are upon until the Day of Resurrection, which is the day of the opening of the barrier of Yajuj and Majuj. ﴿And they, from every elevation, will rush forth﴾ — the pronoun refers to Yajuj and Majuj. "Haddab" is every raised hill of the earth, and its plural is "ahdab," derived from the hump of the earth. The meaning of "yansilun" is "they hasten"; it was also said: "they come out." Al-Zajjaj said: "naslan" is the gait of a wolf when it hastens; one says nasala fulan fi al-ʿadw yansilu, with kasra and damma, nasl-an, nusul-an, and nuslan-an: that is, Yajuj and Majuj will hasten their pace from every elevated place on the earth and disperse across the earth. It was also said: the pronoun in "wa-hum" refers to all creation, and the meaning is that they will be gathered to the place of standing, hastening from every elevated place of the earth. It was read with a damma on the sīn. Al-Mahdawi transmitted this reading from Ibn Masʿud, and al-Tha'labi transmitted this reading as well from Mujahid and Abu al-Sahba'.

﴿And the promise draws near﴾ — it is coordinated (ʿatf) upon "futihat," and what is meant is the reckoning that follows the opening. Al-Farra', al-Kisa'i, and others said: the intended "promise" is the true promise, the Resurrection, and the "wa" is extra; the meaning: until, when Yajuj and Majuj are opened, the true promise, which is the Resurrection, draws near; so "iqtarab" is the answer of "idha." Al-Farra' recited:

So when we passed the courtyard of the tribe and he set his course...

That is, "intaha." From this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And He threw him down upon his forehead﴾ and ﴿We called him﴾ [al-Saffat: 103–104]. Al-Farra' permitted that the answer of "idha" be ﴿then, behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring﴾. Al-Basriyyun said: the answer is omitted, and the estimate is: they will say, "O woe to us!"

The Dhamir in *fa-idha hiya* refers to the story (*al-qissah*), or it is an ambiguous pronoun explained by what follows. *Idha* is used for sudden occurrence (*li-l-mufajaʾah*). Some have said the sentence is complete at His words *hiya*, and the implied construction is: *fa-idha hiya* (meaning) the Resurrection is *barizah* (manifest), *waqiʿah* (having occurred), as if it were *atiyah* (coming) and *hadirah* (present). Then he began and said: *shakhisah absar al-ladhina kafaru* (the eyes of those who disbelieved will be fixed in horror), placing the predicate before the subject, meaning: the eyes of those who disbelieved are fixed in horror. And *ya wayla-na* (woe to us), with an implied verb of saying, [means]: ﴿Indeed, you were in heedlessness of this﴾, that is, of this which has come upon us, of the Resurrection and the Reckoning. ﴿Rather, we were wrongdoers﴾: they retracted the description of themselves as heedless, meaning: we were not heedless, rather we were wrongdoers to ourselves by denying and by not submitting to the Messengers.

Al-Ḥākim narrated it and authenticated it from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words ﴿And We made his wife fit for him﴾, that he said: "The wife of Zakariyya had a problem in her tongue, and Allah rectified it." Something similar was narrated from a group of the Tabiʿun (Successors).

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding the verse, that he said: "We granted him her child."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, who said: "She was barren, so He made her fertile, and He granted him Yahya through her." Regarding His words ﴿And they were humbly submissive to Us﴾, he said: "Humbled."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And they called upon Us in hope and fear﴾. In the reading of Ibn Masʿud: "fa-la kufra li-saʿyihi." ﴿And indeed, We are recording it for him﴾ — that is, We are preserving his effort. Similar to this is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, I do not waste the work of any worker among you, male or female﴾ [Al ʿImran: 195].

﴿And there is a prohibition upon a town which We have destroyed﴾. Zayd ibn Thabit and the people of Madina read "wa-haram," and the people of Kufa read "wa-haram" (with a different vowelling). The first reading was preferred by Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim, and the second reading was transmitted from ʿAli, Ibn Masʿud, and Ibn ʿAbbas; they are two dialects, like ḥill and ḥalal. Saʿid ibn Jubayr read "wa-harima" with a fatha on the ḥāʾ, a kasra on the rāʾ, and a fatha on the mīm. ʿIkrima and Abu al-ʿAliya read "ḥaruma" with a damma on the rāʾ and fatha on the ḥāʾ and mīm. The meaning of "ahlaknaha" is: We decreed its destruction. The clause ﴿that they do not return﴾ is in a position of nominative, either as a subject whose predicate is "ḥaram," or as an agent filling the place of its predicate. The meaning: it is absolutely impossible that they not return to Us for recompense. It was also said: "la" in "la yarji'un" is extra; that is: it is prohibited for a town which We have destroyed that they return to the world after destruction. Abu ʿUbayda chose this. It was also said: "ḥaram" here means "obligatory": that is, obligatory upon a town, and from this is the saying of al-Khansa':

And indeed, "ḥaram" — I do not see anyone weeping over his grief for the rest of time except that I wept over Sakhr.

It was also said: "ḥaram" means "impeded": their return to repentance is impossible, with "la" being extra. Al-Nahhas said: the verse is problematic, and among the best and most majestic things said about it is what Ibn ʿUyayna, Ibn ʿUlayya, Hushaym, Ibn Idris, Muhammad ibn Fadl, Sulaym ibn Hibban, and Mu'alla transmitted from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the meaning of the verse: he said: "it is decreed that they do not return," that is, they do not repent. Al-Zajjaj and Abu ʿAli al-Farisi said: there is an implied element in the speech, that is: "and it is prohibited upon a town for which We have decreed destruction, or the sealing of the hearts of its people, that any deed be accepted from them, because they do not return," that is, they do not repent.

﴿Until, when Yajuj and Majuj are let loose﴾. "Hatta" here is the one after which speech is related, with an omitted noun (al-mudaf). It was also said: this "hatta" is the one indicating a limit (li-l-ghaya). The meaning: those mentioned previously continue in what they are upon until the Day of Resurrection, which is the day of the opening of the barrier of Yajuj and Majuj. ﴿And they, from every elevation, will rush forth﴾ — the pronoun refers to Yajuj and Majuj. "Haddab" is every raised hill of the earth, and its plural is "ahdab," derived from the hump of the earth. The meaning of "yansilun" is "they hasten"; it was also said: "they come out." Al-Zajjaj said: "naslan" is the gait of a wolf when it hastens; one says nasala fulan fi al-ʿadw yansilu, with kasra and damma, nasl-an, nusul-an, and nuslan-an: that is, Yajuj and Majuj will hasten their pace from every elevated place on the earth and disperse across the earth. It was also said: the pronoun in "wa-hum" refers to all creation, and the meaning is that they will be gathered to the place of standing, hastening from every elevated place of the earth. It was read with a damma on the sīn. Al-Mahdawi transmitted this reading from Ibn Masʿud, and al-Tha'labi transmitted this reading as well from Mujahid and Abu al-Sahba'.

﴿And the promise draws near﴾ — it is coordinated (ʿatf) upon "futihat," and what is meant is the reckoning that follows the opening. Al-Farra', al-Kisa'i, and others said: the intended "promise" is the true promise, the Resurrection, and the "wa" is extra; the meaning: until, when Yajuj and Majuj are opened, the true promise, which is the Resurrection, draws near; so "iqtarab" is the answer of "idha." Al-Farra' recited:

So when we passed the courtyard of the tribe and he set his course...

That is, "intaha." From this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And He threw him down upon his forehead﴾ and ﴿We called him﴾ [al-Saffat: 103–104]. Al-Farra' permitted that the answer of "idha" be ﴿then, behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring﴾. Al-Basriyyun said: the answer is omitted, and the estimate is: they will say, "O woe to us!"

The Dhamir in *fa-idha hiya* refers to the story (*al-qissah*), or it is an ambiguous pronoun explained by what follows. *Idha* is used for sudden occurrence (*li-l-mufajaʾah*). Some have said the sentence is complete at His words *hiya*, and the implied construction is: *fa-idha hiya* (meaning) the Resurrection is *barizah* (manifest), *waqiʿah* (having occurred), as if it were *atiyah* (coming) and *hadirah* (present). Then he began and said: *shakhisah absar al-ladhina kafaru* (the eyes of those who disbelieved will be fixed in horror), placing the predicate before the subject, meaning: the eyes of those who disbelieved are fixed in horror. And *ya wayla-na* (woe to us), with an implied verb of saying, [means]: ﴿Indeed, you were in heedlessness of this﴾, that is, of this which has come upon us, of the Resurrection and the Reckoning. ﴿Rather, we were wrongdoers﴾: they retracted the description of themselves as heedless, meaning: we were not heedless, rather we were wrongdoers to ourselves by denying and by not submitting to the Messengers.

Al-Ḥākim narrated it and authenticated it from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words ﴿And We made his wife fit for him﴾, that he said: "The wife of Zakariyya had a problem in her tongue, and Allah rectified it." Something similar was narrated from a group of the Tabiʿun (Successors).

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding the verse, that he said: "We granted him her child."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah, who said: "She was barren, so He made her fertile, and He granted him Yahya through her." Regarding His words ﴿And they were humbly submissive to Us﴾, he said: "Humbled."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Jurayj regarding His words ﴿And they called upon Us in hope and fear﴾, that he said: "Hope in the mercy of Allah and fear of the punishment of Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And they called upon Us in hope and fear﴾. He said: 'Hope, like this, and fear, like this,' and he spread his palms, meaning he placed their backs toward the ground in hope and reversed it in fear."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nuʿaym in *al-Hilyah*, al-Ḥākim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shuʿab* narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUkaym, who said: "Abu Bakr al-Siddiq addressed us, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'Amma baʿd (to proceed). I enjoin you to have taqwa of Allah, and to praise Him with what He is worthy of, and to mix hope with fear, for Allah praised Zakariyya and his family, saying: ﴿Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and call upon Us in hope and fear, and they were humbly submissive to Us﴾.'"

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community﴾, that he said: "Indeed, this is your religion, one religion." Ibn Jarir narrated the like of it from Mujahid. ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar from Qatadah.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Zayd regarding His words ﴿And they cut their affair among themselves into sects﴾, that he said: "*Taqqaʿu* means they differed regarding the religion."

Al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Shuʿab* narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿And there is a prohibition upon a town which We have destroyed﴾, that he said: "It became obligatory to destroy it." ﴿That they will not return﴾: he said: "They will not repent."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated the like of it from ʿIkrimah and Saʿid ibn Jubayr.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿From every slope﴾, that he said: "A height (*sharaf*), they will swarm (*yansilun*)," and he said: "They will advance (*yuqbilun*)." Numerous hadiths have been transmitted concerning the description of Yajuj and Majuj and the time of their emergence, but mentioning them here is of little benefit.

It was also said: she had a bad character, and Allah made her good in character. There is no barrier to intending both matters together: Allah, glorified is He, sets right her person, so she becomes fertile after having been barren, and sets right her character, so her character becomes pleasing after having been displeasing.

The clause ﴿Indeed they used to hasten to good deeds﴾ serves as a reason for what precedes it, namely His kindness, glorified is He, toward His prophets, peace be upon them. The pronoun refers to them. It was also said that it refers to Zakariyya, his wife, and Yahya. Then Allah, glorified is He, described them as those who ﴿call upon Us with longing and fear﴾ — that is, they supplicate to Him in times of ease and in times of hardship. It was also said: "raghab" is raising the palms' inner surfaces toward the sky, and "rahab" is raising their backs. The accusative of "raghaban wa-rahaban" is either as a verbal noun (masdar): that is, they long with longing and fear with fear; or as a reason (ʿilla): that is, for longing and fear; or as a circumstantial state (hal): that is, longing and fearing. Talha ibn Musarrif read "wa-yadʿunana" with a single nun; al-Aʿmash read with a damma on the rāʾ in both words and sukun on what follows; Ibn Wathhab read with a fatha on the rāʾ in both words and a fatha on what follows in both. ﴿And they were humble before Us﴾ — that is, submissive and supplicating.

﴿And she who guarded her chastity (ahsanat farjaha)﴾ — that is, recall her account: she is Maryam (Mary). She guarded her chastity from both the lawful and the unlawful, and no human touched her. He mentioned her alongside the prophets, though she was not among them, because of the mention of ʿIsa (Jesus), and because of the wondrous sign in the account of her. ﴿So We breathed into her of Our Spirit﴾ — Allah, glorified is He, attributed the Spirit to Himself, as an honour and exaltation, and He means the Spirit of ʿIsa. ﴿And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the sign is singular in them, because she bore him without a male. The explanation of similar matters has passed in Surah al-Nisa' and Maryam.

It was also said: the intended meaning is all creation, and that they made their affair in their religions into pieces and divided it among themselves: this one is a monotheist, this one is a Jew, this one is a Christian, this one is a Magian, and this one is an idol-worshipper.
