The second restricts the subject to the predicate, as in your saying *innama Zayd qa'im* (Zayd is only standing), meaning: there is in him only the attribute of standing. ﴿Will you then submit?﴾: will you be submissive, sincere in worship and in the monotheism of God, glorified is He?

﴿But if they turn away﴾: that is, they turn away from Islam, ﴿then say to them: I have announced to you on an equal footing﴾: that is, I have informed you that between us and you there is war, with no reconciliation between us, and I have made the announcement equally, not singling out some of you over others. This is like His words, glorified is He: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them [their treaty] on an equal footing﴾ [al-Anfal: 58], that is, inform them that you have broken the covenant in a way that makes you equal with them in it. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is, I have informed you of what is revealed to me equally in knowledge of it, and I do not reveal to anyone something I have concealed from another. ﴿And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far﴾: that is, I do not know whether what you are promised is near in its occurrence or far away. It is the victory of Islam and its people over disbelief and its people. It was said that what you are promised means the Resurrection. It was also said: I have announced war to you, but I do not know what I will be permitted to do in fighting you.

﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken openly and He knows what you conceal﴾: that is, God, glorified is He, knows what you openly proclaim of disbelief and of attacking Islam and its people, and what you hide and conceal of that. ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you﴾: that is, I do not know; perhaps the respite is a trial for you and a test to see how you act. ﴿And enjoyment for a time﴾: that is, and a provision for a set time that His wisdom requires.

Then God, glorified and exalted is He, related the supplication of His Prophet (ﷺ) with His words: ﴿He said: My Lord, judge with truth﴾: that is, judge between me and these deniers by what is the truth in Your sight. Thus he entrusted the matter to Him, glorified is He. Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa' and Ibn Muhaysin read *Rabbu* with a *damma* on the *ba'*. Al-Nahhas said: this is a grammatical error according to the grammarians, who do not permit *rajulu aqbala* (a man came) but say *ya rajul* (O man). Al-Dahhak, Talhah and Ya'qub read *Ahkamu* with a cut hamza, an open *kaf* and a *damma* on the *mim*, meaning: Muhammad said, "My Lord is the most just in truth." It is also read *Qul* in the imperative, meaning: say, O Muhammad. *Rabbi* is in the accusative position because it is a vocative noun (*munada*) with a pronoun attached. God, glorified is He, answered the supplication of His Prophet (ﷺ), so He punished them at Badr. Then He gave the final outcome, the victory and the triumph, to His believing servants. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.

Then He, glorified is He, said, completing that narration: ﴿And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the One sought for help against what you describe﴾ of disbelief and denial. So *Rabbuna* is the subject and *al-Rahman* is its predicate, meaning He is abundant in mercy toward His servants. *Al-Musta'an* is another predicate, meaning the One sought for help in the matters, among which is what you describe, namely that the power will be yours, and your saying: ﴿Is this not but a human being like you?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 3], and your saying: ﴿The Most Merciful has taken a son﴾ [al-Anbiya': 26; Maryam: 88]. The word *wasf* (description) is often used in the Book of God to mean falsehood, as in His words: ﴿Woe to you for what you describe﴾ [al-Anbiya': 18], and His words: ﴿He will recompense them for their description﴾ [al-An'am: 139]. Al-Mufaddal and al-Sulami read *'ala ma yasifun* with the *ya'* (third person). The rest read it with the *ta'* (second person), as an address.

Al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his *Nasikh* (on abrogation, *naskh*), Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh have related from multiple chains, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will be its entrants﴾, the polytheists said: The angels, Jesus and Uzayr are worshipped besides God. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the good has preceded from Us are removed far from it﴾, meaning Jesus, Uzayr and the angels.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' in *al-Mukhtarah* related from him: "'Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ari came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: You claim that God revealed to you this verse: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will be its entrants.﴾ Ibn al-Zib'ari said: The sun, the moon, the angels, Uzayr and Jesus son of Mary have been worshipped; all of these are in the Fire along with our gods." Then this was revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, your people turn away from it and say: Are our gods better, or he? They cite it to you only for argument. Rather, they are a contentious people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 57–58]. Then this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the good has preceded from Us are removed far from it.﴾

Abu Dawud in his *Nasikh* and Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani related from another route from him, similar to it, but longer.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His words: "(p-951) ﴿Indeed, those for whom the good has preceded from Us﴾", that they are Jesus, Uzayr and the angels.

Ibn Jarir related from him also, concerning His words ﴿fuel of Hell﴾ [hasab jahannam], that it is the trees of Hell. In its chain is al-'Awfi. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him from another route that *hasab jahannam* is its fuel. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also, saying: it is the firewood of Hell in the Zanji (Ethiopian) language.

Ibn Mardawayh related from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His words ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾, that it is serpents on the Path (al-Sirat) that say "hass hass" (a sound of pain).

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, concerning His words ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾, that it is serpents on the Path that sting them, and when they sting them, they say "hass hass".

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir related from Muhammad ibn Hatib, who said: 'Ali was asked about this verse, ﴿Indeed, those for whom the good has preceded from Us﴾, and he said: It is 'Uthman and his companions.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾, that he said: the people of Paradise will not hear the sound of the Fire when they descend to their place from Paradise.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾, that he said: it is the final blast. In its chain is al-'Awfi.

Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, who graded it good (hasan), related from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Three will be on mounds of musk; the greatest terror on the Day of Resurrection will not frighten them: a man who led a people in prayer while they were pleased with him; a man who called the adhan every day and night; and a servant who fulfilled the right of God and the right of his masters."

Abd ibn Humayd related from 'Ali, concerning His words ﴿Like the rolling of the scroll (al-sijill)﴾, that he said: it is an angel. Abd ibn Humayd related similarly from 'Atiyyah. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Umar, who said: *al-sijill* is an angel; when he ascends with the seeking of forgiveness, he says: "Write it as light."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn 'Asakir related from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, who said: *al-sijill* is an angel.

Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mandah in *al-Ma'rifah*, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his *Sunan*, who graded it sound, related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: *al-sijill* was a scribe of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn 'Adi and Ibn 'Asakir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had a scribe called al-Sijill," and this is His words: ﴿On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of the scroll for documents﴾. He said: Just as the scroll rolls up the document, so We roll up the heaven.

Ibn Mandah and Abu Nu'aym in *al-Ma'rifah*, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Khatib and Ibn 'Asakir related from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) had a scribe called al-Sijill, so God revealed: ﴿On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of the scroll for documents.﴾"

Ibn Kathir said in his *Tafsir*, after citing this hadith: This is extremely munkar (rejected) from the hadith of Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar; it is not sound at all. He said: Likewise what preceded from Ibn 'Abbas through the narration of Abu Dawud and others is not sound either. A group of the memorizers (huffaz) has explicitly declared it fabricated, although it is in the Sunan of Abu Dawud. Among them is our shaykh, the great memorizer Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi. I have devoted a separate part to this hadith, and praise be to God.

He said: The Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir undertook to reject this hadith and refuted it most thoroughly, and said: We do not know of any companion named Sijill, and the scribes of the Prophet (ﷺ) were well known, and none of them was named al-Sijill. May God have mercy on him; he was right in that, and it is among the strongest proofs of the rejection of this hadith. As for whoever mentioned this among the names of the companions, he relied only on this hadith and nothing else, and God knows best.

He said: The sound report from Ibn 'Abbas is that *al-sijill* is the sheet (*sahifah*), as related by 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-'Awfi from him. This was affirmed by Mujahid, Qatadah and others, and Ibn Jarir chose it because it is the known meaning in the language. On this view, the meaning of the statement is: On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of the scroll for the book, that is, over the book, meaning the written, as in His words: ﴿And when they had both submitted, and he put him down upon his forehead﴾ [al-Saffat: 103], that is, upon the forehead. There are parallels to this in the language, and God knows best.

I (al-Shawkani) say: As for this being the sound report from Ibn 'Abbas, it is not so, for 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-'Awfi are weak. So it is better to rely on the linguistic meaning and to adopt it. Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: *al-sijill* is the man. Ibn Mardawayh added: in the language of Ethiopia. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the interpretation of the verse, that he said: like the rolling of the page over the book.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it﴾, that he said: We will destroy everything as it was the first time.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him, concerning His words ﴿And We had certainly written in the Zabur after the reminder﴾, that he said: "the Qur'an," that the earth is the land of Paradise. Ibn Jarir also related from him, concerning ﴿And We had certainly written in the Zabur﴾, that he said: "the books," and ﴿after the reminder﴾, he said: "the Torah." In its chain is al-'Awfi. Sa'id ibn Mansur also related from him, who said: The Zabur, the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an.

The Reminder (al-Dhikr) is the original from which these books were copied, which is in heaven. And the earth is the earth of Paradise.

Al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him (Ibn Abbas) regarding His saying ﴿that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ that he said: it is the earth of Paradise.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him regarding the verse that he said: Allah, glorified is He, informed in the Tawrah (Torah) and the Zabur (Psalms), and in His prior decree before the heavens and the earth were created, that He would give the earth as an inheritance to the community of Muhammad and admit them into Paradise, and they are the righteous. And regarding His saying ﴿Surely in this is a message for a people who worship﴾ he said: those who have knowledge. In its chain is Ali ibn Abi Talha.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Abu Hurayrah regarding ﴿Surely in this is a message for a people who worship﴾ that he said: the five daily prayers.

Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym and al-Daylami related from Anas that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Regarding the saying of Allah, ﴿Surely in this is a message for a people who worship﴾, He said: in the five daily prayers, an occupation for worship."

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse, ﴿a message for a people who worship﴾, and said: it is the five daily prayers in the Sacred Mosque in congregation.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il related from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ that he said: whoever believes, the mercy is complete for him in this world and the Hereafter, and whoever does not believe is spared what befell the (earlier) nations in this world of punishments such as sinking into the earth, transformation, and hurling (of stones).

Muslim related from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "It was said, O Messenger of Allah, invoke Allah against the polytheists. He said: 'I was not sent as a curser, but I was sent only as a mercy.'"

al-Tayalisi, Ahmad, al-Tabarani and Abu Nu'aym in al-Dala'il related from Abu Umamah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah sent me as a mercy to the worlds and a guidance to the God-fearing."

Ahmad and al-Tabarani related from Salman that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whichever man of my community I revile with a reviling in my anger, or whom I curse with a curse, I am only a man from the children of Adam; I get angry as they get angry. But Allah sent me only as a mercy to the worlds, so make it for him a blessing on the Day of Resurrection."

al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il related from Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am only a mercy bestowed." The meaning of this has been related through several chains.

Ibn Abi Khaythamah and Ibn Asakir related from al-Rabi' ibn Anas that he said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) was taken on the night journey, he saw a certain man, who was one of the Banu Umayyah, on the pulpit delivering a sermon to the people, and that grieved the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah revealed ﴿And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a time﴾, meaning: this kingship."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you﴾ that he said: what He informed you of regarding the punishment and the Hour; perhaps the delay of that is a trial for you.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him regarding His saying ﴿He said: My Lord, judge with truth﴾ that he said: Allah judges only with truth, and he (the Prophet) was only hastening toward that in this world, asking his Lord.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 21, verses 98–112 (part 1 of 3):

.
He, glory be to Him, described the state of their objects of worship on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾. This is an address from Him, glory be to Him, to the people of Makkah, and what is meant by His words "what you worship" is the idols that they used to worship.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read ḥaṣab with the unpointed ṣād, meaning the fuel and firewood of Hell. Everything with which you kindle the fire or stir it up is a ḥaṣab; so said al-Jawhari. Abu 'Ubaydah said: everything you throw into the fire, you have fed it with (ḥaṣabtahā) by it, and similar to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So fear the Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾ [al-Baqarah: 24]. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and 'Aishah read ḥaṭab (ḥaṭab) of Hell with the ṭā', and Ibn 'Abbas read ḥaḍab with the dotted ḍād. Al-Farra' said: it has been related to us that ḥaḍab in the dialect of the people of Yemen means firewood. The purpose of casting the idols into the Fire, although they are inanimate things that neither understand nor feel it, is to rebuke those who worshipped them, to increase the reproach directed at them, and to double their grief over them. It has also been said that they will be heated and then pressed against them, as an increase in their punishment. The clause ﴿you are going to it as arrivers﴾ is either a new (independent) sentence or a substitute (badal) for "the fuel of Hell"; the address is to them and to what they worship, by way of predominance (taghlib). The lām in "lahā" is for emphasis, because the active participle is weak in its government; it has also been said that it means ʿalā (upon). The meaning of "arrival" (al-wurud) here is entering. Many of the people of knowledge said: ʿĪsā, ʿUzayr and the angels do not enter into this verse, because "mā" is used for what does not understand, and had He intended generality He would have said "man" (who) you worship. Al-Zajjaj said: and also because those addressed in this verse are the polytheists of Makkah and no others.

﴿Had these been gods, they would not have entered it﴾: that is, had these idols been gods as you claim, they would not have entered it; that is, the worshippers and the worshipped would not have entered the Fire. It has also been said: only the worshippers would not have entered it, but they did enter it, so they were not gods. In this there is rebuke for the idol-worshippers and severe reproach. ﴿And each of them will abide therein forever﴾: that is, every one of the worshippers and the worshipped will abide in the Fire forever, not coming out of it.

﴿For them therein is a groaning (zafīr)﴾: that is, for these who have entered the Fire. Zafīr is the sound of the breath of one in distress, and what is meant here is moaning and intense breathing; its explanation has already been given in Hud. ﴿And they therein will not hear﴾: that is, some of them will not hear the groaning of others because of the intensity of the terror. It has also been said: they will hear nothing, because they will be gathered deaf, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And We shall gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, dumb and deaf﴾ [al-Isra': 97]. Hearing is taken from them because in it there is some comfort and companionship. It has also been said: they will not hear what pleases them, but will hear what grieves them.

Then, after He, glory be to Him, had explained the state of these wretched ones, He began to explain the state of the blessed, saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best (al-ḥusnā) has preceded from Us﴾: that is, the best attribute, which is the best of qualities, and it is felicity; it has also been said: success (tawfīq), or the good tidings of Paradise, or Paradise itself. ﴿Those will be kept far from it﴾: a reference to those described by that quality, kept far from it, that is, from Hell, because they have already come to be in Paradise.

﴿They will not hear its faintest sound (ḥasīs)﴾: al-ḥissu and al-ḥasīs is the sound you hear from a thing that passes close by you. The meaning: they will not hear the movement of the Fire or the movement of its people. This clause is either a substitute for "kept far" or a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from its pronoun. ﴿And they, in what their souls desire, will abide forever﴾: that is, they will remain permanently; and in Paradise there is what the souls desire and what the eyes delight in, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And for you therein is what your souls desire, and for you therein is what you ask for﴾ [Fussilat: 31].

﴿The great terror will not grieve them﴾: Abu Ja'far and Ibn Muhaysin read (lā yuḥzinuhum) with a ḍammah on the yā' and a kasrah on the zā', while the rest read ﴿lā yaḥzunuhumu﴾ with a fatḥah on the yā' and a ḍammah on the zā'. Al-Yazidi said: ḥazanahu is the dialect of Quraysh, and aḥzanahu is the dialect of Tamim. "The great terror" means the horrors of the Day of Resurrection: the Resurrection, the reckoning and the punishment. ﴿And the angels will receive them﴾: that is, they will meet them at the gates of Paradise, congratulating them and saying to them: ﴿This is your day which you were promised﴾: that is, you were promised it in the world and given good tidings of what is in it. Thus said a group of the exegetes: that what is meant by His words "Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us" up to here is all those described by faith and righteous deeds, not the Messiah, ʿUzayr and the angels. But most of the exegetes said: when the verse ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship﴾ was revealed, Ibn al-Zibaʿrā came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, do you not claim that ʿUzayr is a righteous man, and ʿĪsā is a righteous man, and Maryam is a righteous woman?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then the angels, ʿĪsā, ʿUzayr and Maryam are worshipped besides Allah, so these are in the Fire." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾. The account of who transmitted this will come shortly, if Allah wills.

﴿On the day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of a scroll for writings﴾: Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa', Shaybah, al-A'raj and al-Zuhri read (tuṭwā) with a feminine dotted-above ta' and a ḍammah, with the sky in the nominative case; Mujahid read (yaṭwī) with an open yā' beneath, in the active voice, meaning Allah rolls up the sky; and the rest read ﴿naṭwī﴾ with the plural "we" of majesty, and "the day" is in the accusative, governed by His saying "We shall repeat it," meaning: We shall repeat it on the day We roll up the heaven. It has also been said that it is a substitute for the omitted pronoun in "you were promised," and the sense is: those you were promised it on the day We roll up. It has been said it is governed by "the great terror will not grieve them," and said to be governed by "the angels will receive them." It has been said it is linked to an omitted verb, which is "remember," and this is the most evident and clearest view. Ṭayy is the opposite of spreading out (nashr). It has been said it means erasure. What is meant by "the heaven" is the class (genus). Sijill means the document: that is, rolled up like the rolling of a scroll (ṭūmār). It has been said that sijill means a deed, and it is derived from al-musājalah, which is writing and correspondence, and its root is from al-sajl, which is a bucket; one says: "I drew (sājaltu) the man" when you draw a bucket and he draws a bucket. Then the word was borrowed for correspondence and exchange in speech, and from this is the saying of al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿUtbah ibn Abi Lahab:

"Whoever contends with me, let him contend with a noble man who fills the bucket up to the knot of the rope."

Abu Zur'ah ibn 'Amr and Ibn Jarir read (al-sujull) with a ḍammah on the sīn and the jīm and a shaddah on the lām; al-A'mash and Talhah read with a fatḥah on the sīn, a sukūn on the jīm and a light lām. The ṭayy in this verse may bear two meanings: one is ṭayy which is the opposite of spreading, and from it is His saying: ﴿And the heavens are rolled up in His right hand﴾ [al-Zumar: 67]. The second is concealment, obscuring and erasure, because Allah, glory be to Him, erases and effaces its traces and dims its stars. It has also been said: sijill is the name of an angel, who rolls up the books of the children of Adam; it has also been said: it is the name of a scribe of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the first is more preferable. Al-A'mash, Hafs, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Yahya and Khalaf read "li-l-kutub" (for the books) all together, while the rest read "li-l-kitāb" (for the writing). It is linked to an omitted element, and is a circumstantial clause from sijill: that is, like the rolling of a scroll, existing for the books; or an attribute of it: that is, the one existing for the books, since "the books" is an expression for the pages and what is written in them, so the sijill is part of their parts, and the rolling properly applies to it. As for the second reading, al-kitāb is a verbal noun, and the lām indicates purpose: that is, as a scroll is rolled up for writing, that it may be written in, or for the many meanings that are written in it. This is on the assumption that what is meant by the rolling is the first meaning, which is the opposite of spreading. ﴿As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it﴾: that is, as We began creating them in the wombs of their mothers and brought them out to the earth barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, so likewise We shall return them on the Day of Resurrection. "First creation" is the object of "We shall repeat," the omitted object being explained by the mentioned "We shall repeat it"; or it is the object of "began," and "mā" is either a restrictive particle or a relative pronoun, and the kāf is connected to an omitted element, meaning: We shall repeat the like of what We began, We shall repeat it. In this way "first" (awwal) is an adverb of time for "began," or a circumstantial. The first creation is singled out for mention to portray the bringing into existence from non-existence, and the intended aim is to demonstrate the validity of return by analogy with the beginning, since both share the essential possibility. It has also been said: the meaning of the verse is: We shall destroy every soul as it was the first time; on this view the speech is connected to His saying "the day We roll up the heaven." It has also been said: the meaning is: We shall change the heaven, then We shall repeat it a second time after its rolling and passing away; but the first is preferable, and it is like His saying: ﴿And indeed you have come to Us alone as We created you the first time﴾ [al-An'am: 94]. Then He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿A promise upon Us; indeed We are ever doing﴾. The accusative of "a promise" is as a verbal noun: that is, We promised a promise upon Us, its fulfilment and the keeping of it, which is the resurrection and the repetition. Then He, glory be to Him, emphasized that with His saying: ﴿Indeed We are ever doing﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "indeed We are ever doing" is: indeed We have always been capable of what We will. It has also been said: indeed We have always been doing what We promised you, and like it is His saying: ﴿His promise was ever fulfilled﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 18].

105 ﴿And We have certainly written in the Psalms﴾: the zubur, in origin, are books; one says zabartu, meaning I wrote. On this basis it is valid to apply "al-Zabur" to the Torah and the Gospel, and to the book of Dawud called the Zabur. It has also been said that what is meant here is the book of Dawud. The meaning of ﴿after the Reminder﴾ is: after the Preserved Tablet. It has also been said it is the Torah: that is, by Allah, We have certainly written in the book of Dawud after what We wrote in the Torah, or after what We wrote in the Preserved Tablet ﴿that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: al-Zabur is the plural of books: the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an, because al-Zabur and al-Kitab have one meaning; one says zabartu and katabtu. What he said is supported by Hamzah's reading of "al-Zubur" with a ḍammah on the zā', for it is the plural of zubur. The meaning of ﴿My righteous servants will inherit it﴾ has been disputed. It has been said the intended meaning is the land of Paradise, and those who hold this view cite His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say: Praise be to Allah who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the earth﴾ [al-Zumar: 74]. It has been said it is the Holy Land. It has been said it is the land of the disbelieving nations, which our Prophet (ﷺ) and his community will inherit by conquest. It has been said (p-950) that what is meant is the Children of Israel, on the evidence of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made the people who were oppressed inherit the eastern and western parts of the earth which We had blessed﴾ [al-A'raf: 137]. The apparent meaning is that this is good tidings to the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) of inheriting the lands of the disbelievers, and this is the view of most exegetes. Hamzah read "ʿibādī" with the yā' sukūn, and the rest read it with the yā' vowelled.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 21, verses 98–112 (part 2 of 3):

﴿Indeed, in this is a sufficient message﴾: that is, in what has been mentioned in this surah of admonition and warning is a message, meaning sufficiency. It is said of such a thing, *balagh*, *bulgha* and *tabligh*, meaning sufficiency. It was also said that the reference in His words "Indeed, in this" is to the Qur'an, ﴿for a people who worship﴾, that is, who are occupied with worshipping God and concerned with it. *Ibadah* (worship) is submission and humility, and they are the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). The foremost of worship is the prayer. ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾: that is, We have not sent you, O Muhammad, with the laws and rulings except as a mercy to all people. The exception here is an *istithna' mufarragh* (an exception with no stated category), drawn from the most general of circumstances and causes: that is, We did not send you for any cause among the causes except for Our vast mercy, for what you were sent with is a means to the happiness of both abodes. It was said that the meaning of his being a mercy to the disbelievers is that they were safe through him from being swallowed up by the earth, transformed, or annihilated. It was also said that by "the worlds" is meant only the believers, but the first view is preferable, based on His words, glorified is He: ﴿And God would not punish them while you are among them﴾ [al-Anfal: 33].

Then He, glorified is He, explained that the root of that mercy is monotheism and disavowal of association, so He said: ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God is one God. Will you then submit?﴾ If *ma* is a relative pronoun (*mawsulah*), the meaning is: what is revealed to me is that His attribute is restricted to oneness, not exceeding it to what contradicts or opposes it. If *ma* is a restrictive particle (*kafffah*), the meaning is: the revelation to me is restricted to God's exclusive possession of unity. The reason for this is that restriction (*qasr*) always applies to what follows *innama*. The first *innama* restricts the predicate to the subject, as in your saying *innama yaqumu Zayd* (only Zayd stands), meaning: no one stands except Zayd. The second restricts the subject to the predicate, as in your saying *innama Zayd qa'im* (Zayd is only standing), meaning: there is in him only the attribute of standing. ﴿Will you then submit?﴾: will you be submissive, sincere in worship and in the monotheism of God, glorified is He?

﴿But if they turn away﴾: that is, they turn away from Islam, ﴿then say to them: I have announced to you on an equal footing﴾: that is, I have informed you that between us and you there is war, with no reconciliation between us, and I have made the announcement equally, not singling out some of you over others. This is like His words, glorified is He: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them [their treaty] on an equal footing﴾ [al-Anfal: 58], that is, inform them that you have broken the covenant in a way that makes you equal with them in it. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is, I have informed you of what is revealed to me equally in knowledge of it, and I do not reveal to anyone something I have concealed from another. ﴿And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far﴾: that is, I do not know whether what you are promised is near in its occurrence or far away. It is the victory of Islam and its people over disbelief and its people. It was said that what you are promised means the Resurrection. It was also said: I have announced war to you, but I do not know what I will be permitted to do in fighting you.

﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken openly and He knows what you conceal﴾: that is, God, glorified is He, knows what you openly proclaim of disbelief and of attacking Islam and its people, and what you hide and conceal of that. ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you﴾: that is, I do not know; perhaps the respite is a trial for you and a test to see how you act. ﴿And enjoyment for a time﴾: that is, and a provision for a set time that His wisdom requires.

Then God, glorified and exalted is He, related the supplication of His Prophet (ﷺ) with His words: ﴿He said: My Lord, judge with truth﴾: that is, judge between me and these deniers by what is the truth in Your sight. Thus he entrusted the matter to Him, glorified is He. Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa' and Ibn Muhaysin read *Rabbu* with a *damma* on the *ba'*. Al-Nahhas said: this is a grammatical error according to the grammarians, who do not permit *rajulu aqbala* (a man came) but say *ya rajul* (O man). Al-Dahhak, Talhah and Ya'qub read *Ahkamu* with a cut hamza, an open *kaf* and a *damma* on the *mim*, meaning: Muhammad said, "My Lord is the most just in truth." It is also read *Qul* in the imperative, meaning: say, O Muhammad. *Rabbi* is in the accusative position because it is a vocative noun (*munada*) with a pronoun attached. God, glorified is He, answered the supplication of His Prophet (ﷺ), so He punished them at Badr. Then He gave the final outcome, the victory and the triumph, to His believing servants. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.

Then He, glorified is He, said, completing that narration: ﴿And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the One sought for help against what you describe﴾ of disbelief and denial. So *Rabbuna* is the subject and *al-Rahman* is its predicate, meaning He is abundant in mercy toward His servants. *Al-Musta'an* is another predicate, meaning the One sought for help in the matters, among which is what you describe, namely that the power will be yours, and your saying: ﴿Is this not but a human being like you?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 3], and your saying: ﴿The Most Merciful has taken a son﴾ [al-Anbiya': 26; Maryam: 88]. The word *wasf* (description) is often used in the Book of God to mean falsehood, as in His words: ﴿Woe to you for what you describe﴾ [al-Anbiya': 18], and His words: ﴿He will recompense them for their description﴾ [al-An'am: 139]. Al-Mufaddal and al-Sulami read *'ala ma yasifun* with the *ya'* (third person). The rest read it with the *ta'* (second person), as an address.

Al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his *Nasikh* (on abrogation, *naskh*), Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh have related from multiple chains, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will be its entrants﴾, the polytheists said: The angels, Jesus and Uzayr are worshipped besides God. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the good has preceded from Us are removed far from it﴾, meaning Jesus, Uzayr and the angels.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' in *al-Mukhtarah* related from him: "'Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ari came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: You claim that God revealed to you this verse: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will be its entrants.﴾ Ibn al-Zib'ari said: The sun, the moon, the angels, Uzayr and Jesus son of Mary have been worshipped; all of these are in the Fire along with our gods." Then this was revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, your people turn away from it and say: Are our gods better, or he? They cite it to you only for argument. Rather, they are a contentious people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 57–58]. Then this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the good has preceded from Us are removed far from it.﴾

Abu Dawud in his *Nasikh* and Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani related from another route from him, similar to it, but longer.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His words: "(p-951) ﴿Indeed, those for whom the good has preceded from Us﴾", that they are Jesus, Uzayr and the angels.

Ibn Jarir related from him also, concerning His words ﴿fuel of Hell﴾ [hasab jahannam], that it is the trees of Hell. In its chain is al-'Awfi. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him from another route that *hasab jahannam* is its fuel. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also, saying: it is the firewood of Hell in the Zanji (Ethiopian) language.

Ibn Mardawayh related from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His words ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾, that it is serpents on the Path (al-Sirat) that say "hass hass" (a sound of pain).

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, concerning His words ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾, that it is serpents on the Path that sting them, and when they sting them, they say "hass hass".

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir related from Muhammad ibn Hatib, who said: 'Ali was asked about this verse, ﴿Indeed, those for whom the good has preceded from Us﴾, and he said: It is 'Uthman and his companions.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾, that he said: the people of Paradise will not hear the sound of the Fire when they descend to their place from Paradise.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾, that he said: it is the final blast. In its chain is al-'Awfi.

Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, who graded it good (hasan), related from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Three will be on mounds of musk; the greatest terror on the Day of Resurrection will not frighten them: a man who led a people in prayer while they were pleased with him; a man who called the adhan every day and night; and a servant who fulfilled the right of God and the right of his masters."

Abd ibn Humayd related from 'Ali, concerning His words ﴿Like the rolling of the scroll (al-sijill)﴾, that he said: it is an angel. Abd ibn Humayd related similarly from 'Atiyyah. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Umar, who said: *al-sijill* is an angel; when he ascends with the seeking of forgiveness, he says: "Write it as light."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn 'Asakir related from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, who said: *al-sijill* is an angel.

Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mandah in *al-Ma'rifah*, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his *Sunan*, who graded it sound, related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: *al-sijill* was a scribe of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn 'Adi and Ibn 'Asakir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had a scribe called al-Sijill," and this is His words: ﴿On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of the scroll for documents﴾. He said: Just as the scroll rolls up the document, so We roll up the heaven.

Ibn Mandah and Abu Nu'aym in *al-Ma'rifah*, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Khatib and Ibn 'Asakir related from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) had a scribe called al-Sijill, so God revealed: ﴿On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of the scroll for documents.﴾"

Ibn Kathir said in his *Tafsir*, after citing this hadith: This is extremely munkar (rejected) from the hadith of Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar; it is not sound at all. He said: Likewise what preceded from Ibn 'Abbas through the narration of Abu Dawud and others is not sound either. A group of the memorizers (huffaz) has explicitly declared it fabricated, although it is in the Sunan of Abu Dawud. Among them is our shaykh, the great memorizer Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi. I have devoted a separate part to this hadith, and praise be to God.

He said: The Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir undertook to reject this hadith and refuted it most thoroughly, and said: We do not know of any companion named Sijill, and the scribes of the Prophet (ﷺ) were well known, and none of them was named al-Sijill. May God have mercy on him; he was right in that, and it is among the strongest proofs of the rejection of this hadith. As for whoever mentioned this among the names of the companions, he relied only on this hadith and nothing else, and God knows best.

He said: The sound report from Ibn 'Abbas is that *al-sijill* is the sheet (*sahifah*), as related by 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-'Awfi from him. This was affirmed by Mujahid, Qatadah and others, and Ibn Jarir chose it because it is the known meaning in the language. On this view, the meaning of the statement is: On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of the scroll for the book, that is, over the book, meaning the written, as in His words: ﴿And when they had both submitted, and he put him down upon his forehead﴾ [al-Saffat: 103], that is, upon the forehead. There are parallels to this in the language, and God knows best.

I (al-Shawkani) say: As for this being the sound report from Ibn 'Abbas, it is not so, for 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-'Awfi are weak. So it is better to rely on the linguistic meaning and to adopt it. Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: *al-sijill* is the man. Ibn Mardawayh added: in the language of Ethiopia. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the interpretation of the verse, that he said: like the rolling of the page over the book.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it﴾, that he said: We will destroy everything as it was the first time.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him, concerning His words ﴿And We had certainly written in the Zabur after the reminder﴾, that he said: "the Qur'an," that the earth is the land of Paradise. Ibn Jarir also related from him, concerning ﴿And We had certainly written in the Zabur﴾, that he said: "the books," and ﴿after the reminder﴾, he said: "the Torah." In its chain is al-'Awfi. Sa'id ibn Mansur also related from him, who said: The Zabur, the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an.

The Reminder (al-Dhikr) is the original from which these books were copied, which is in heaven. And the earth is the earth of Paradise.

Al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him (Ibn Abbas) regarding His saying ﴿that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ that he said: it is the earth of Paradise.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him regarding the verse that he said: Allah, glorified is He, informed in the Tawrah (Torah) and the Zabur (Psalms), and in His prior decree before the heavens and the earth were created, that He would give the earth as an inheritance to the community of Muhammad and admit them into Paradise, and they are the righteous. And regarding His saying ﴿Surely in this is a message for a people who worship﴾ he said: those who have knowledge. In its chain is Ali ibn Abi Talha.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Abu Hurayrah regarding ﴿Surely in this is a message for a people who worship﴾ that he said: the five daily prayers.

Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym and al-Daylami related from Anas that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Regarding the saying of Allah, ﴿Surely in this is a message for a people who worship﴾, He said: in the five daily prayers, an occupation for worship."

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse, ﴿a message for a people who worship﴾, and said: it is the five daily prayers in the Sacred Mosque in congregation.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il related from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ that he said: whoever believes, the mercy is complete for him in this world and the Hereafter, and whoever does not believe is spared what befell the (earlier) nations in this world of punishments such as sinking into the earth, transformation, and hurling (of stones).

Muslim related from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "It was said, O Messenger of Allah, invoke Allah against the polytheists. He said: 'I was not sent as a curser, but I was sent only as a mercy.'"

al-Tayalisi, Ahmad, al-Tabarani and Abu Nu'aym in al-Dala'il related from Abu Umamah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah sent me as a mercy to the worlds and a guidance to the God-fearing."

Ahmad and al-Tabarani related from Salman that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whichever man of my community I revile with a reviling in my anger, or whom I curse with a curse, I am only a man from the children of Adam; I get angry as they get angry. But Allah sent me only as a mercy to the worlds, so make it for him a blessing on the Day of Resurrection."

al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il related from Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am only a mercy bestowed." The meaning of this has been related through several chains.

Ibn Abi Khaythamah and Ibn Asakir related from al-Rabi' ibn Anas that he said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) was taken on the night journey, he saw a certain man, who was one of the Banu Umayyah, on the pulpit delivering a sermon to the people, and that grieved the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah revealed ﴿And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a time﴾, meaning: this kingship."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you﴾ that he said: what He informed you of regarding the punishment and the Hour; perhaps the delay of that is a trial for you.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him regarding His saying ﴿He said: My Lord, judge with truth﴾ that he said: Allah judges only with truth, and he (the Prophet) was only hastening toward that in this world, asking his Lord.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 21, verses 98–112 (part 1 of 3):

.
He, glory be to Him, described the state of their objects of worship on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾. This is an address from Him, glory be to Him, to the people of Makkah, and what is meant by His words "what you worship" is the idols that they used to worship.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read ḥaṣab with the unpointed ṣād, meaning the fuel and firewood of Hell. Everything with which you kindle the fire or stir it up is a ḥaṣab; so said al-Jawhari. Abu 'Ubaydah said: everything you throw into the fire, you have fed it with (ḥaṣabtahā) by it, and similar to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So fear the Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾ [al-Baqarah: 24]. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and 'Aishah read ḥaṭab (ḥaṭab) of Hell with the ṭā', and Ibn 'Abbas read ḥaḍab with the dotted ḍād. Al-Farra' said: it has been related to us that ḥaḍab in the dialect of the people of Yemen means firewood. The purpose of casting the idols into the Fire, although they are inanimate things that neither understand nor feel it, is to rebuke those who worshipped them, to increase the reproach directed at them, and to double their grief over them. It has also been said that they will be heated and then pressed against them, as an increase in their punishment. The clause ﴿you are going to it as arrivers﴾ is either a new (independent) sentence or a substitute (badal) for "the fuel of Hell"; the address is to them and to what they worship, by way of predominance (taghlib). The lām in "lahā" is for emphasis, because the active participle is weak in its government; it has also been said that it means ʿalā (upon). The meaning of "arrival" (al-wurud) here is entering. Many of the people of knowledge said: ʿĪsā, ʿUzayr and the angels do not enter into this verse, because "mā" is used for what does not understand, and had He intended generality He would have said "man" (who) you worship. Al-Zajjaj said: and also because those addressed in this verse are the polytheists of Makkah and no others.

﴿Had these been gods, they would not have entered it﴾: that is, had these idols been gods as you claim, they would not have entered it; that is, the worshippers and the worshipped would not have entered the Fire. It has also been said: only the worshippers would not have entered it, but they did enter it, so they were not gods. In this there is rebuke for the idol-worshippers and severe reproach. ﴿And each of them will abide therein forever﴾: that is, every one of the worshippers and the worshipped will abide in the Fire forever, not coming out of it.

﴿For them therein is a groaning (zafīr)﴾: that is, for these who have entered the Fire. Zafīr is the sound of the breath of one in distress, and what is meant here is moaning and intense breathing; its explanation has already been given in Hud. ﴿And they therein will not hear﴾: that is, some of them will not hear the groaning of others because of the intensity of the terror. It has also been said: they will hear nothing, because they will be gathered deaf, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And We shall gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, dumb and deaf﴾ [al-Isra': 97]. Hearing is taken from them because in it there is some comfort and companionship. It has also been said: they will not hear what pleases them, but will hear what grieves them.

Then, after He, glory be to Him, had explained the state of these wretched ones, He began to explain the state of the blessed, saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best (al-ḥusnā) has preceded from Us﴾: that is, the best attribute, which is the best of qualities, and it is felicity; it has also been said: success (tawfīq), or the good tidings of Paradise, or Paradise itself. ﴿Those will be kept far from it﴾: a reference to those described by that quality, kept far from it, that is, from Hell, because they have already come to be in Paradise.

﴿They will not hear its faintest sound (ḥasīs)﴾: al-ḥissu and al-ḥasīs is the sound you hear from a thing that passes close by you. The meaning: they will not hear the movement of the Fire or the movement of its people. This clause is either a substitute for "kept far" or a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from its pronoun. ﴿And they, in what their souls desire, will abide forever﴾: that is, they will remain permanently; and in Paradise there is what the souls desire and what the eyes delight in, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And for you therein is what your souls desire, and for you therein is what you ask for﴾ [Fussilat: 31].

﴿The great terror will not grieve them﴾: Abu Ja'far and Ibn Muhaysin read (lā yuḥzinuhum) with a ḍammah on the yā' and a kasrah on the zā', while the rest read ﴿lā yaḥzunuhumu﴾ with a fatḥah on the yā' and a ḍammah on the zā'. Al-Yazidi said: ḥazanahu is the dialect of Quraysh, and aḥzanahu is the dialect of Tamim. "The great terror" means the horrors of the Day of Resurrection: the Resurrection, the reckoning and the punishment. ﴿And the angels will receive them﴾: that is, they will meet them at the gates of Paradise, congratulating them and saying to them: ﴿This is your day which you were promised﴾: that is, you were promised it in the world and given good tidings of what is in it. Thus said a group of the exegetes: that what is meant by His words "Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us" up to here is all those described by faith and righteous deeds, not the Messiah, ʿUzayr and the angels. But most of the exegetes said: when the verse ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship﴾ was revealed, Ibn al-Zibaʿrā came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, do you not claim that ʿUzayr is a righteous man, and ʿĪsā is a righteous man, and Maryam is a righteous woman?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then the angels, ʿĪsā, ʿUzayr and Maryam are worshipped besides Allah, so these are in the Fire." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾. The account of who transmitted this will come shortly, if Allah wills.

﴿On the day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of a scroll for writings﴾: Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa', Shaybah, al-A'raj and al-Zuhri read (tuṭwā) with a feminine dotted-above ta' and a ḍammah, with the sky in the nominative case; Mujahid read (yaṭwī) with an open yā' beneath, in the active voice, meaning Allah rolls up the sky; and the rest read ﴿naṭwī﴾ with the plural "we" of majesty, and "the day" is in the accusative, governed by His saying "We shall repeat it," meaning: We shall repeat it on the day We roll up the heaven. It has also been said that it is a substitute for the omitted pronoun in "you were promised," and the sense is: those you were promised it on the day We roll up. It has been said it is governed by "the great terror will not grieve them," and said to be governed by "the angels will receive them." It has been said it is linked to an omitted verb, which is "remember," and this is the most evident and clearest view. Ṭayy is the opposite of spreading out (nashr). It has been said it means erasure. What is meant by "the heaven" is the class (genus). Sijill means the document: that is, rolled up like the rolling of a scroll (ṭūmār). It has been said that sijill means a deed, and it is derived from al-musājalah, which is writing and correspondence, and its root is from al-sajl, which is a bucket; one says: "I drew (sājaltu) the man" when you draw a bucket and he draws a bucket. Then the word was borrowed for correspondence and exchange in speech, and from this is the saying of al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿUtbah ibn Abi Lahab:

"Whoever contends with me, let him contend with a noble man who fills the bucket up to the knot of the rope."

Abu Zur'ah ibn 'Amr and Ibn Jarir read (al-sujull) with a ḍammah on the sīn and the jīm and a shaddah on the lām; al-A'mash and Talhah read with a fatḥah on the sīn, a sukūn on the jīm and a light lām. The ṭayy in this verse may bear two meanings: one is ṭayy which is the opposite of spreading, and from it is His saying: ﴿And the heavens are rolled up in His right hand﴾ [al-Zumar: 67]. The second is concealment, obscuring and erasure, because Allah, glory be to Him, erases and effaces its traces and dims its stars. It has also been said: sijill is the name of an angel, who rolls up the books of the children of Adam; it has also been said: it is the name of a scribe of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the first is more preferable. Al-A'mash, Hafs, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Yahya and Khalaf read "li-l-kutub" (for the books) all together, while the rest read "li-l-kitāb" (for the writing). It is linked to an omitted element, and is a circumstantial clause from sijill: that is, like the rolling of a scroll, existing for the books; or an attribute of it: that is, the one existing for the books, since "the books" is an expression for the pages and what is written in them, so the sijill is part of their parts, and the rolling properly applies to it. As for the second reading, al-kitāb is a verbal noun, and the lām indicates purpose: that is, as a scroll is rolled up for writing, that it may be written in, or for the many meanings that are written in it. This is on the assumption that what is meant by the rolling is the first meaning, which is the opposite of spreading. ﴿As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it﴾: that is, as We began creating them in the wombs of their mothers and brought them out to the earth barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, so likewise We shall return them on the Day of Resurrection. "First creation" is the object of "We shall repeat," the omitted object being explained by the mentioned "We shall repeat it"; or it is the object of "began," and "mā" is either a restrictive particle or a relative pronoun, and the kāf is connected to an omitted element, meaning: We shall repeat the like of what We began, We shall repeat it. In this way "first" (awwal) is an adverb of time for "began," or a circumstantial. The first creation is singled out for mention to portray the bringing into existence from non-existence, and the intended aim is to demonstrate the validity of return by analogy with the beginning, since both share the essential possibility. It has also been said: the meaning of the verse is: We shall destroy every soul as it was the first time; on this view the speech is connected to His saying "the day We roll up the heaven." It has also been said: the meaning is: We shall change the heaven, then We shall repeat it a second time after its rolling and passing away; but the first is preferable, and it is like His saying: ﴿And indeed you have come to Us alone as We created you the first time﴾ [al-An'am: 94]. Then He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿A promise upon Us; indeed We are ever doing﴾. The accusative of "a promise" is as a verbal noun: that is, We promised a promise upon Us, its fulfilment and the keeping of it, which is the resurrection and the repetition. Then He, glory be to Him, emphasized that with His saying: ﴿Indeed We are ever doing﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "indeed We are ever doing" is: indeed We have always been capable of what We will. It has also been said: indeed We have always been doing what We promised you, and like it is His saying: ﴿His promise was ever fulfilled﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 18].

105 ﴿And We have certainly written in the Psalms﴾: the zubur, in origin, are books; one says zabartu, meaning I wrote. On this basis it is valid to apply "al-Zabur" to the Torah and the Gospel, and to the book of Dawud called the Zabur. It has also been said that what is meant here is the book of Dawud. The meaning of ﴿after the Reminder﴾ is: after the Preserved Tablet. It has also been said it is the Torah: that is, by Allah, We have certainly written in the book of Dawud after what We wrote in the Torah, or after what We wrote in the Preserved Tablet ﴿that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: al-Zabur is the plural of books: the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an, because al-Zabur and al-Kitab have one meaning; one says zabartu and katabtu. What he said is supported by Hamzah's reading of "al-Zubur" with a ḍammah on the zā', for it is the plural of zubur. The meaning of ﴿My righteous servants will inherit it﴾ has been disputed. It has been said the intended meaning is the land of Paradise, and those who hold this view cite His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say: Praise be to Allah who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the earth﴾ [al-Zumar: 74]. It has been said it is the Holy Land. It has been said it is the land of the disbelieving nations, which our Prophet (ﷺ) and his community will inherit by conquest. It has been said (p-950) that what is meant is the Children of Israel, on the evidence of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made the people who were oppressed inherit the eastern and western parts of the earth which We had blessed﴾ [al-A'raf: 137]. The apparent meaning is that this is good tidings to the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) of inheriting the lands of the disbelievers, and this is the view of most exegetes. Hamzah read "ʿibādī" with the yā' sukūn, and the rest read it with the yā' vowelled.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 21, verses 98–112 (part 2 of 3):

﴿Indeed, in this is a sufficient message﴾: that is, in what has been mentioned in this surah of admonition and warning is a message, meaning sufficiency. It is said of such a thing, *balagh*, *bulgha* and *tabligh*, meaning sufficiency. It was also said that the reference in His words "Indeed, in this" is to the Qur'an, ﴿for a people who worship﴾, that is, who are occupied with worshipping God and concerned with it. *Ibadah* (worship) is submission and humility, and they are the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). The foremost of worship is the prayer. ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾: that is, We have not sent you, O Muhammad, with the laws and rulings except as a mercy to all people. The exception here is an *istithna' mufarragh* (an exception with no stated category), drawn from the most general of circumstances and causes: that is, We did not send you for any cause among the causes except for Our vast mercy, for what you were sent with is a means to the happiness of both abodes. It was said that the meaning of his being a mercy to the disbelievers is that they were safe through him from being swallowed up by the earth, transformed, or annihilated. It was also said that by "the worlds" is meant only the believers, but the first view is preferable, based on His words, glorified is He: ﴿And God would not punish them while you are among them﴾ [al-Anfal: 33].

Then He, glorified is He, explained that the root of that mercy is monotheism and disavowal of association, so He said: ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God is one God. Will you then submit?﴾ If *ma* is a relative pronoun (*mawsulah*), the meaning is: what is revealed to me is that His attribute is restricted to oneness, not exceeding it to what contradicts or opposes it. If *ma* is a restrictive particle (*kafffah*), the meaning is: the revelation to me is restricted to God's exclusive possession of unity. The reason for this is that restriction (*qasr*) always applies to what follows *innama*. The first *innama* restricts the predicate to the subject, as in your saying *innama yaqumu Zayd* (only Zayd stands), meaning: no one stands except Zayd. The second restricts the subject to the predicate, as in your saying *innama Zayd qa'im* (Zayd is only standing), meaning: there is in him only the attribute of standing. ﴿Will you then submit?﴾: will you be submissive, sincere in worship and in the monotheism of God, glorified is He?

﴿But if they turn away﴾: that is, they turn away from Islam, ﴿then say to them: I have announced to you on an equal footing﴾: that is, I have informed you that between us and you there is war, with no reconciliation between us, and I have made the announcement equally, not singling out some of you over others. This is like His words, glorified is He: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them [their treaty] on an equal footing﴾ [al-Anfal: 58], that is, inform them that you have broken the covenant in a way that makes you equal with them in it. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is, I have informed you of what is revealed to me equally in knowledge of it, and I do not reveal to anyone something I have concealed from another. ﴿And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far﴾: that is, I do not know whether what you are promised is near in its occurrence or far away. It is the victory of Islam and its people over disbelief and its people. It was said that what you are promised means the Resurrection. It was also said: I have announced war to you, but I do not know what I will be permitted to do in fighting you.

﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken openly and He knows what you conceal﴾: that is, God, glorified is He, knows what you openly proclaim of disbelief and of attacking Islam and its people, and what you hide and conceal of that. ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you﴾: that is, I do not know; perhaps the respite is a trial for you and a test to see how you act. ﴿And enjoyment for a time﴾: that is, and a provision for a set time that His wisdom requires.

Then God, glorified and exalted is He, related the supplication of His Prophet (ﷺ) with His words: ﴿He said: My Lord, judge with truth﴾: that is, judge between me and these deniers by what is the truth in Your sight. Thus he entrusted the matter to Him, glorified is He. Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa' and Ibn Muhaysin read *Rabbu* with a *damma* on the *ba'*. Al-Nahhas said: this is a grammatical error according to the grammarians, who do not permit *rajulu aqbala* (a man came) but say *ya rajul* (O man). Al-Dahhak, Talhah and Ya'qub read *Ahkamu* with a cut hamza, an open *kaf* and a *damma* on the *mim*, meaning: Muhammad said, "My Lord is the most just in truth." It is also read *Qul* in the imperative, meaning: say, O Muhammad. *Rabbi* is in the accusative position because it is a vocative noun (*munada*) with a pronoun attached. God, glorified is He, answered the supplication of His Prophet (ﷺ), so He punished them at Badr. Then He gave the final outcome, the victory and the triumph, to His believing servants. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.

Then He, glorified is He, said, completing that narration: ﴿And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the One sought for help against what you describe﴾ of disbelief and denial. So *Rabbuna* is the subject and *al-Rahman* is its predicate, meaning He is abundant in mercy toward His servants. *Al-Musta'an* is another predicate, meaning the One sought for help in the matters, among which is what you describe, namely that the power will be yours, and your saying: ﴿Is this not but a human being like you?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 3], and your saying: ﴿The Most Merciful has taken a son﴾ [al-Anbiya': 26; Maryam: 88]. The word *wasf* (description) is often used in the Book of God to mean falsehood, as in His words: ﴿Woe to you for what you describe﴾ [al-Anbiya': 18], and His words: ﴿He will recompense them for their description﴾ [al-An'am: 139]. Al-Mufaddal and al-Sulami read *'ala ma yasifun* with the *ya'* (third person). The rest read it with the *ta'* (second person), as an address.

Al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his *Nasikh* (on abrogation, *naskh*), Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh have related from multiple chains, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will be its entrants﴾, the polytheists said: The angels, Jesus and Uzayr are worshipped besides God. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the good has preceded from Us are removed far from it﴾, meaning Jesus, Uzayr and the angels.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' in *al-Mukhtarah* related from him: "'Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ari came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: You claim that God revealed to you this verse: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will be its entrants.﴾ Ibn al-Zib'ari said: The sun, the moon, the angels, Uzayr and Jesus son of Mary have been worshipped; all of these are in the Fire along with our gods." Then this was revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, your people turn away from it and say: Are our gods better, or he? They cite it to you only for argument. Rather, they are a contentious people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 57–58]. Then this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the good has preceded from Us are removed far from it.﴾

Abu Dawud in his *Nasikh* and Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani related from another route from him, similar to it, but longer.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His words: "(p-951) ﴿Indeed, those for whom the good has preceded from Us﴾", that they are Jesus, Uzayr and the angels.

Ibn Jarir related from him also, concerning His words ﴿fuel of Hell﴾ [hasab jahannam], that it is the trees of Hell. In its chain is al-'Awfi. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him from another route that *hasab jahannam* is its fuel. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also, saying: it is the firewood of Hell in the Zanji (Ethiopian) language.

Ibn Mardawayh related from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His words ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾, that it is serpents on the Path (al-Sirat) that say "hass hass" (a sound of pain).

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, concerning His words ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾, that it is serpents on the Path that sting them, and when they sting them, they say "hass hass".

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir related from Muhammad ibn Hatib, who said: 'Ali was asked about this verse, ﴿Indeed, those for whom the good has preceded from Us﴾, and he said: It is 'Uthman and his companions.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾, that he said: the people of Paradise will not hear the sound of the Fire when they descend to their place from Paradise.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾, that he said: it is the final blast. In its chain is al-'Awfi.

Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, who graded it good (hasan), related from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Three will be on mounds of musk; the greatest terror on the Day of Resurrection will not frighten them: a man who led a people in prayer while they were pleased with him; a man who called the adhan every day and night; and a servant who fulfilled the right of God and the right of his masters."

Abd ibn Humayd related from 'Ali, concerning His words ﴿Like the rolling of the scroll (al-sijill)﴾, that he said: it is an angel. Abd ibn Humayd related similarly from 'Atiyyah. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Umar, who said: *al-sijill* is an angel; when he ascends with the seeking of forgiveness, he says: "Write it as light."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn 'Asakir related from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, who said: *al-sijill* is an angel.

Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mandah in *al-Ma'rifah*, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his *Sunan*, who graded it sound, related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: *al-sijill* was a scribe of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn 'Adi and Ibn 'Asakir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had a scribe called al-Sijill," and this is His words: ﴿On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of the scroll for documents﴾. He said: Just as the scroll rolls up the document, so We roll up the heaven.

Ibn Mandah and Abu Nu'aym in *al-Ma'rifah*, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Khatib and Ibn 'Asakir related from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) had a scribe called al-Sijill, so God revealed: ﴿On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of the scroll for documents.﴾"

Ibn Kathir said in his *Tafsir*, after citing this hadith: This is extremely munkar (rejected) from the hadith of Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar; it is not sound at all. He said: Likewise what preceded from Ibn 'Abbas through the narration of Abu Dawud and others is not sound either. A group of the memorizers (huffaz) has explicitly declared it fabricated, although it is in the Sunan of Abu Dawud. Among them is our shaykh, the great memorizer Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi. I have devoted a separate part to this hadith, and praise be to God.

He said: The Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir undertook to reject this hadith and refuted it most thoroughly, and said: We do not know of any companion named Sijill, and the scribes of the Prophet (ﷺ) were well known, and none of them was named al-Sijill. May God have mercy on him; he was right in that, and it is among the strongest proofs of the rejection of this hadith. As for whoever mentioned this among the names of the companions, he relied only on this hadith and nothing else, and God knows best.

He said: The sound report from Ibn 'Abbas is that *al-sijill* is the sheet (*sahifah*), as related by 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-'Awfi from him. This was affirmed by Mujahid, Qatadah and others, and Ibn Jarir chose it because it is the known meaning in the language. On this view, the meaning of the statement is: On the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling of the scroll for the book, that is, over the book, meaning the written, as in His words: ﴿And when they had both submitted, and he put him down upon his forehead﴾ [al-Saffat: 103], that is, upon the forehead. There are parallels to this in the language, and God knows best.

I (al-Shawkani) say: As for this being the sound report from Ibn 'Abbas, it is not so, for 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-'Awfi are weak. So it is better to rely on the linguistic meaning and to adopt it. Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: *al-sijill* is the man. Ibn Mardawayh added: in the language of Ethiopia. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the interpretation of the verse, that he said: like the rolling of the page over the book.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it﴾, that he said: We will destroy everything as it was the first time.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him, concerning His words ﴿And We had certainly written in the Zabur after the reminder﴾, that he said: "the Qur'an," that the earth is the land of Paradise. Ibn Jarir also related from him, concerning ﴿And We had certainly written in the Zabur﴾, that he said: "the books," and ﴿after the reminder﴾, he said: "the Torah." In its chain is al-'Awfi. Sa'id ibn Mansur also related from him, who said: The Zabur, the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an.

The Reminder (al-Dhikr) is the original from which these books were copied, which is in heaven. And the earth is the earth of Paradise.

Al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him (Ibn Abbas) regarding His saying ﴿that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ that he said: it is the earth of Paradise.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him regarding the verse that he said: Allah, glorified is He, informed in the Tawrah (Torah) and the Zabur (Psalms), and in His prior decree before the heavens and the earth were created, that He would give the earth as an inheritance to the community of Muhammad and admit them into Paradise, and they are the righteous. And regarding His saying ﴿Surely in this is a message for a people who worship﴾ he said: those who have knowledge. In its chain is Ali ibn Abi Talha.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Abu Hurayrah regarding ﴿Surely in this is a message for a people who worship﴾ that he said: the five daily prayers.

Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym and al-Daylami related from Anas that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Regarding the saying of Allah, ﴿Surely in this is a message for a people who worship﴾, He said: in the five daily prayers, an occupation for worship."

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse, ﴿a message for a people who worship﴾, and said: it is the five daily prayers in the Sacred Mosque in congregation.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il related from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ that he said: whoever believes, the mercy is complete for him in this world and the Hereafter, and whoever does not believe is spared what befell the (earlier) nations in this world of punishments such as sinking into the earth, transformation, and hurling (of stones).

Muslim related from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "It was said, O Messenger of Allah, invoke Allah against the polytheists. He said: 'I was not sent as a curser, but I was sent only as a mercy.'"

al-Tayalisi, Ahmad, al-Tabarani and Abu Nu'aym in al-Dala'il related from Abu Umamah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah sent me as a mercy to the worlds and a guidance to the God-fearing."

Ahmad and al-Tabarani related from Salman that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whichever man of my community I revile with a reviling in my anger, or whom I curse with a curse, I am only a man from the children of Adam; I get angry as they get angry. But Allah sent me only as a mercy to the worlds, so make it for him a blessing on the Day of Resurrection."

al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il related from Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am only a mercy bestowed." The meaning of this has been related through several chains.

Ibn Abi Khaythamah and Ibn Asakir related from al-Rabi' ibn Anas that he said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) was taken on the night journey, he saw a certain man, who was one of the Banu Umayyah, on the pulpit delivering a sermon to the people, and that grieved the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah revealed ﴿And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a time﴾, meaning: this kingship."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you﴾ that he said: what He informed you of regarding the punishment and the Hour; perhaps the delay of that is a trial for you.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him regarding His saying ﴿He said: My Lord, judge with truth﴾ that he said: Allah judges only with truth, and he (the Prophet) was only hastening toward that in this world, asking his Lord.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 21, verses 98–112 (part 1 of 3):

.
He, glory be to Him, described the state of their objects of worship on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾. This is an address from Him, glory be to Him, to the people of Makkah, and what is meant by His words "what you worship" is the idols that they used to worship.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read ḥaṣab with the unpointed ṣād, meaning the fuel and firewood of Hell. Everything with which you kindle the fire or stir it up is a ḥaṣab; so said al-Jawhari. Abu 'Ubaydah said: everything you throw into the fire, you have fed it with (ḥaṣabtahā) by it, and similar to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So fear the Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾ [al-Baqarah: 24]. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and 'Aishah read ḥaṭab (ḥaṭab) of Hell with the ṭā', and Ibn 'Abbas read ḥaḍab with the dotted ḍād. Al-Farra' said: it has been related to us that ḥaḍab in the dialect of the people of Yemen means firewood. The purpose of casting the idols into the Fire, although they are inanimate things that neither understand nor feel it, is to rebuke those who worshipped them, to increase the reproach directed at them, and to double their grief over them. It has also been said that they will be heated and then pressed against them, as an increase in their punishment. The clause ﴿you are going to it as arrivers﴾ is either a new (independent) sentence or a substitute (badal) for "the fuel of Hell"; the address is to them and to what they worship, by way of predominance (taghlib). The lām in "lahā" is for emphasis, because the active participle is weak in its government; it has also been said that it means ʿalā (upon). The meaning of "arrival" (al-wurud) here is entering. Many of the people of knowledge said: ʿĪsā, ʿUzayr and the angels do not enter into this verse, because "mā" is used for what does not understand, and had He intended generality He would have said "man" (who) you worship. Al-Zajjaj said: and also because those addressed in this verse are the polytheists of Makkah and no others.

﴿Had these been gods, they would not have entered it﴾: that is, had these idols been gods as you claim, they would not have entered it; that is, the worshippers and the worshipped would not have entered the Fire. It has also been said: only the worshippers would not have entered it, but they did enter it, so they were not gods.
